+"""
+EduAgent Interview Coach — Final Report Generator & Study Analytics
+===================================================================
+
+Generates comprehensive, structured post-interview performance summaries,
+separating verified demonstrated strengths from unresolved gaps, and produces
+prioritized DSA revision recommendations per PRD FR-16 and TRD Section 13.1.
+"""
+
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Union
+
+from interview_engine import InterviewSession
+
+
+class ReportGenerator:
+    """
+    Synthesizes session attempt records and concept mastery state into an
+    actionable evaluation report and markdown summary.
+    """
+
+    DISCLAIMER_TEXT = (
+        "This report provides practice feedback to support technical interview preparation. "
+        "It is designed for self-assessment and does not guarantee specific interview or hiring outcomes."
+    )
+
+    RECOMMENDATION_CATALOG = {
+        "underflow": (
+            "Practice empty-collection edge cases: Always verify that size > 0 before calling pop() "
+            "or dequeue() to prevent underflow exceptions."
+        ),
+        "overflow": (
+            "Review bounded capacity handling: Ensure fixed-size arrays check size == capacity "
+            "before pushing or enqueuing to prevent overflow."
+        ),
+        "modulo": (
+            "Master circular queue index calculations: Use modular arithmetic ((index + 1) % capacity) "
+            "for smooth pointer wraparound without element shifting."
+        ),
+        "circular": (
+            "Study circular queue pointer mechanics: Differentiate full vs empty conditions "
+            "(e.g., maintaining an explicit count variable or keeping one slot empty)."
+        ),
+        "two stacks": (
+            "Practice implementing a queue with two stacks: Understand why transferring elements from "
+            "in_stack to out_stack yields amortized O(1) dequeue operations."
+        ),
+        "monotonic": (
+            "Explore monotonic stack problems (e.g., Next Greater Element or Daily Temperatures) "
+            "to understand how pruning elements achieves linear O(n) total runtime."
+        ),
+        "complexity": (
+            "Review amortized vs worst-case analysis: While dynamic array resizing takes O(n) rarely, "
+            "its amortized cost per push remains O(1)."
+        ),
+        "lifo": (
+            "Reinforce the LIFO principle: Elements are added and removed from the same end (the top). "
+            "Ideal for recursion, call stacks, and parenthesis matching."
+        ),
+        "fifo": (
+            "Reinforce the FIFO principle: Elements enter at the rear and exit from the front. "
+            "Essential for breadth-first search (BFS) and asynchronous task scheduling."
+        ),
+    }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def generate_report(
+        cls, session: Union[InterviewSession, Dict[str, Any]]
+    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+        """
+        Builds the complete final evaluation report dictionary.
+        Accepts either an InterviewSession instance or its dictionary representation.
+        """
+        if isinstance(session, InterviewSession):
+            data = session.to_dict()
+            total_score = session.total_score
+            avg_score = session.average_score
+        elif isinstance(session, dict):
+            data = session
+            attempts = data.get("attempts", [])
+            valid_attempts = [
+                a for a in attempts
+                if isinstance(a.get("evaluation"), dict) and "score" in a["evaluation"]
+            ]
+            total_score = sum(a["evaluation"]["score"] for a in valid_attempts)
+            avg_score = (
+                round(total_score / len(valid_attempts), 1) if valid_attempts else 0.0
+            )
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Expected InterviewSession or dict, got {type(session).__name__}")
+
+        attempts = data.get("attempts", [])
+        attempts_count = len(attempts)
+        max_possible = attempts_count * 10
+        percentage = round((total_score / max_possible) * 100, 1) if max_possible > 0 else 0.0
+
+        # Performance Tier classification
+        if attempts_count == 0:
+            tier = "Incomplete"
+            tier_summary = "No questions completed in this session."
+        elif percentage >= 80.0:
+            tier = "Proficient"
+            tier_summary = "Strong conceptual mastery of Stacks and Queues with sound technical reasoning."
+        elif percentage >= 50.0:
+            tier = "Developing"
+            tier_summary = "Good foundational knowledge with some missing operation mechanics or edge cases."
+        else:
+            tier = "Foundational"
+            tier_summary = "Core concepts need reinforcement, particularly around basic definitions and operations."
+
+        demonstrated = sorted(list(data.get("demonstrated_concepts", [])))
+        unresolved = sorted(list(data.get("unresolved_concepts", [])))
+
+        # Extract specific misconceptions from attempts
+        misconceptions = []
+        for att in attempts:
+            eval_dict = att.get("evaluation", {})
+            for m in eval_dict.get("misconceptions", []):
+                if m not in misconceptions:
+                    misconceptions.append(m)
+
+        recommendations = cls._generate_recommendations(unresolved, misconceptions, tier)
+
+        # Question attempt summaries
+        question_summaries = []
+        for idx, att in enumerate(attempts, 1):
+            eval_info = att.get("evaluation", {})
+            question_summaries.append({
+                "number": idx,
+                "question_id": att.get("question_id", "unknown"),
+                "question_text": att.get("question_text", ""),
+                "topic": att.get("topic", "DSA"),
+                "difficulty": att.get("difficulty", "medium"),
+                "score": eval_info.get("score", 0),
+                "hint_used": att.get("hint_used", False),
+                "feedback": eval_info.get("feedback", ""),
+            })
+
+        return {
+            "session_id": data.get("session_id", "unknown"),
+            "created_at": data.get("created_at", ""),
+            "evaluation_mode": data.get("evaluation_provider", "local"),
+            "attempts_count": attempts_count,
+            "total_score": total_score,
+            "max_possible_score": max_possible,
+            "average_score": avg_score,
+            "percentage": percentage,
+            "performance_tier": tier,
+            "tier_summary": tier_summary,
+            "hints_used": data.get("hints_used_count", 0),
+            "demonstrated_concepts": demonstrated,
+            "unresolved_concepts": unresolved,
+            "misconceptions_detected": misconceptions,
+            "recommendations": recommendations,
+            "question_summaries": question_summaries,
+            "disclaimer": cls.DISCLAIMER_TEXT,
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def generate_markdown_report(cls, report: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+        """
+        Formats the report dictionary as clean, readable Markdown for UI or export.
+        """
+        lines = [
+            f"# EduAgent Interview Performance Report",
+            f"**Session ID:** `{report['session_id']}`  |  **Evaluation Mode:** `{report['evaluation_mode']}`",
+            "",
+            "## 1. Overall Performance",
+            f"- **Performance Tier:** **{report['performance_tier']}**",
+            f"- **Score:** **{report['total_score']} / {report['max_possible_score']}** ({report['percentage']}%)",
+            f"- **Average Score per Question:** **{report['average_score']} / 10**",
+            f"- **Questions Completed:** {report['attempts_count']}",
+            f"- **Hints Requested:** {report['hints_used']}",
+            f"- **Summary:** {report['tier_summary']}",
+            "",
+            "## 2. Demonstrated Strengths",
+        ]
+
+        if report["demonstrated_concepts"]:
+            for concept in report["demonstrated_concepts"]:
+                lines.append(f"- :white_check_mark: **{concept}**")
+        else:
+            lines.append("- *No concepts were fully demonstrated in this session.*")
+
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append("## 3. Areas for Practice")
+
+        if report["unresolved_concepts"]:
+            for concept in report["unresolved_concepts"]:
+                lines.append(f"- :mag: {concept}")
+        else:
+            lines.append("- :sparkles: *No outstanding concept gaps were recorded.*")
+
+        if report["misconceptions_detected"]:
+            lines.append("")
+            lines.append("### Misconceptions Detected")
+            for m in report["misconceptions_detected"]:
+                lines.append(f"- :warning: **{m}**")
+
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append("## 4. Priority Revision Recommendations")
+        for idx, rec in enumerate(report["recommendations"], 1):
+            lines.append(f"{idx}. {rec}")
+
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append("---")
+        lines.append(f"> *{report['disclaimer']}*")
+
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _generate_recommendations(
+        cls,
+        unresolved_concepts: List[str],
+        misconceptions: List[str],
+        tier: str,
+    ) -> List[str]:
+        """Maps unresolved concepts and misconceptions to prioritized study recommendations."""
+        recommendations: List[str] = []
+        combined_text = " ".join(unresolved_concepts + misconceptions).lower()
+
+        for keyword, advice in cls.RECOMMENDATION_CATALOG.items():
+            if keyword in combined_text:
+                if advice not in recommendations:
+                    recommendations.append(advice)
+
+        # Ensure general recommendations if few specific ones were matched
+        if len(recommendations) < 2:
+            if tier == "Foundational":
+                recommendations.append(
+                    "Start by diagramming Stacks and Queues on paper: Draw push/pop from the top for Stacks, "
+                    "and enqueue at the rear / dequeue from the front for Queues."
+                )
+                recommendations.append(
+                    "Review array-based vs linked-list implementations to understand how pointer movement works."
+                )
+            else:
+                recommendations.append(
+                    "Practice tracing real-world interview applications: Balanced parentheses using a stack, "
+                    "and breadth-first search (BFS) level-order traversal using a queue."
+                )
+                recommendations.append(
+                    "Focus on explaining time complexity tradeoffs aloud: Why linked list vs dynamic array "
+                    "both achieve O(1) amortized stack operations."
+                )
+
+        return recommendations[:5]

+8. **Explain unfamiliar code.** Provide beginner-friendly explanations of important logic, functions, classes, dependencies, and design decisions.

+11. **Protect secrets.** Never write API keys, access tokens, passwords, or other credentials into this log.
+12. **Do not overwrite history.** Add new entries instead of silently replacing earlier entries. Correct mistakes with a dated clarification.
+13. **Ask before risky changes.** Seek approval before destructive operations, broad refactoring, removing important functionality, or changing the agreed project scope.

+#### I. Beginner-friendly explanation

+- **What is a Virtual Environment (`.venv`)?**
+  A virtual environment is an isolated folder on your computer that holds Python packages just for this project. Without it, packages are installed globally, which can break other Python programs if different projects need different versions of the same library.
+- **What is `requirements.txt`?**
+  Think of `requirements.txt` as a project recipe. It lists the exact libraries needed (Streamlit for web interface, Pytest for testing) and safe version boundaries. Anyone opening this project can install everything in one command: `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
+- **What is `.gitignore`?**
+  Git tracks code and documentation changes. However, compiled Python files (`__pycache__`), virtual environments (`.venv`), and private passwords/API keys (`.env`) should never be saved into Git history. The `.gitignore` file gives Git a blacklist of files and directories to ignore automatically.

For example, every question in EduAgent must have an `id`, a `question` text, a list of `expected_points`, and links to `follow_up_ids`. If a question were missing one of these fields, the application might crash in the middle of an interview.
+- **Why do we test Referential Integrity?**
+  In our adaptive interview, when a student finishes question `stack_001`, the system looks at its `follow_up_ids` (`stack_002`, `stack_003`) to pick the next question. Referential integrity testing ensures that every linked question ID actually exists in `question_bank.json`. This guarantees the app will never try to load a question that doesn't exist.
+- **Why test for Negative Cases?**
+  Writing automated tests that purposefully feed bad data (like duplicate IDs or missing fields) into our validator confirms that our safety checks actually catch errors rather than silently letting corrupted data through.

+#### I. Beginner-friendly explanation

+- **Why break scores into four categories?**
+  In an interview, saying "your answer gets 7/10" is not enough to help someone learn. By breaking the score into **Technical Correctness** (is it factually true?), **Key Concepts** (did you mention the core computer science terms?), **Reasoning** (did you explain *why* it works?), and **Clarity** (is the explanation easy to read?), students know exactly what they did well and what they need to improve.
+- **Why must a critical misconception cap the score?**
+  Imagine a candidate who writes: *"A queue is Last In First Out (LIFO). You add to the front and remove from the same end."* If a naive AI simply counts the words "queue", "add", and "remove", it might award a high score. But the candidate fundamentally misunderstands how a queue works! Our evaluator catches this critical misconception, caps the score to 4 or below, and prescribes a simpler follow-up question to re-teach the basics.
+- **What is Schema Validation?**
+  Before any evaluation result is passed to the interview screen, `validate_evaluation_result` checks that the score is a real integer between 0 and 10, that the component points add up to the total, and that all required fields exist. This prevents invalid numbers or missing data from ever crashing the web interface.

+  A standard quiz is static: question 1, then question 2, then question 3, no matter what you wrote. In a real technical interview, a good interviewer listens to what you say. If you give a great answer, they challenge you with a harder follow-up. If you miss an important detail (like the "pop" operation), they ask you about that specific detail next. If you get confused about LIFO vs FIFO, they step back and help you with the basics. Our `AdaptiveEngine` does exactly this using clear, predictable Python rules.
+- **How do we prevent Infinite Loops?**
+  In our question bank, question A links to question B, and question B might link back to question A. To make sure the app never gets stuck repeating the same questions in a loop, the engine tracks `asked_question_ids`. Every time it looks for a question to ask next, it strictly ignores any question that is already in that list. When all questions have been asked, it gracefully concludes the interview!

+#### I. Beginner-friendly explanation
+
+- **What is an MCP Tool?**
+  In the Model Context Protocol, a "tool" is a callable function that an AI agent (such as an Alexa+ skill or an autonomous coding assistant) can invoke. For example, when an Alexa+ assistant wants to test a student on Stacks, it doesn't need to invent questions or pretend to grade them. Instead, it calls `get_interview_question` to retrieve a real question, and then calls `evaluate_student_answer` with what the student spoke or typed. EduAgent does the deterministic grading and gives the assistant the exact rubric breakdown!
+- **How does JSON-RPC 2.0 work?**
+  JSON-RPC 2.0 is a simple, standardized protocol for sending requests and receiving responses using plain JSON text. A client sends a message like:
+  `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "get_interview_question", "arguments": {"question_id": "stack_001"}}}`.
+  Our server processes the request and responds:
+  `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]}}`.
+  Because this follows the open MCP standard, any MCP-compatible AI agent in the world can connect to EduAgent without any custom integration code!

+"""
+test_evaluator.py — Automated Unit Tests for Answer Evaluation Engine
+
+Tests the 10-point scoring rubric, misconception detection, empty answer handling,
+bounds checking, and schema validation.
+"""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import pytest
+from evaluator import (
+    evaluate_answer,
+    validate_evaluation_result,
+    LocalEvaluator,
+    EvaluationResult
+)
+
+QUESTION_BANK_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "question_bank.json"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def questions():
+    with open(QUESTION_BANK_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        data = json.load(f)
+    return {q["id"]: q for q in data}
+
+
+def test_strong_stack_answer(questions):
+    """Verify strong response scores 8-10, recommends progress, and has no misconceptions."""
+    q = questions["stack_001"]
+    answer = (
+        "LIFO stands for Last In First Out, meaning the last element added is the first one removed. "
+        "The push operation adds a new item onto the top of the stack. "
+        "The pop operation removes and returns the top element from the stack. "
+        "This is because access is strictly restricted to the top end."
+    )
+    result = evaluate_answer(q, answer)
+
+    assert 8 <= result["score"] <= 10, f"Expected 8-10 for strong answer, got {result['score']}"
+    assert result["recommended_action"] == "progress"
+    assert len(result["misconceptions"]) == 0
+    assert len(result["correct_points"]) >= 2
+    assert result["score"] == sum(result["score_breakdown"].values())
+
+
+def test_partial_stack_answer(questions):
+    """Verify partial answer scores 5-7, identifies missing concepts, and recommends targeted follow-up."""
+    q = questions["stack_001"]
+    # Answer only explains push, missing pop and formal LIFO definition
+    answer = "Push adds a new element onto the top of the stack."
+    result = evaluate_answer(q, answer)
+
+    assert 3 <= result["score"] <= 7, f"Expected 3-7 for partial answer, got {result['score']}"
+    assert len(result["missing_concepts"]) > 0, "Missing concepts must be identified"
+    assert result["recommended_action"] in {"targeted_follow_up", "scaffold_hint"}
+    assert result["score"] == sum(result["score_breakdown"].values())
+
+
+def test_critical_misconception_detection(questions):
+    """Verify that a critical misconception is caught, penalized, and triggers scaffold hint."""
+    q = questions["stack_001"]
+    # Answer contains the critical misconception: pop removes the oldest element
+    answer = (
+        "In a stack, push adds an item to the top, but the pop operation removes the oldest or bottom element."
+    )
+    result = evaluate_answer(q, answer)
+
+    assert len(result["misconceptions"]) > 0, "Expected misconception to be detected"
+    assert any("oldest or bottom" in m for m in result["misconceptions"])
+    assert result["score"] <= 5, f"Score with critical misconception should be penalized, got {result['score']}"
+    assert result["recommended_action"] == "scaffold_hint"
+    assert result["score"] == sum(result["score_breakdown"].values())
+
+
+def test_empty_and_whitespace_answer(questions):
+    """Verify empty or whitespace answers score 0 and provide clear feedback."""
+    q = questions["stack_001"]
+
+    for empty_input in ["", "   ", "\n\t"]:
+        result = evaluate_answer(q, empty_input)
+        assert result["score"] == 0
+        assert result["score_breakdown"]["technical_correctness"] == 0
+        assert result["score_breakdown"]["key_concepts"] == 0
+        assert result["score_breakdown"]["reasoning"] == 0
+        assert result["score_breakdown"]["clarity"] == 0
+        assert result["recommended_action"] == "scaffold_hint"
+        assert "Write an answer before submitting" in result["feedback"]
+        assert len(result["missing_concepts"]) == len(q["expected_points"])
+
+
+def test_strong_queue_answer(questions):
+    """Verify strong Queue answer scores 8-10 with progress action."""
+    q = questions["queue_001"]
+    answer = (
+        "FIFO means First In, First Out: the first element inserted is the first one removed. "
+        "Enqueue inserts an element at the rear of the queue, while dequeue removes and returns "
+        "the element at the front of the queue, preserving arrival order."
+    )
+    result = evaluate_answer(q, answer)
+
+    assert 8 <= result["score"] <= 10
+    assert result["recommended_action"] == "progress"
+    assert len(result["misconceptions"]) == 0
+    assert result["score"] == sum(result["score_breakdown"].values())
+
+
+def test_queue_misconception_detection(questions):
+    """Verify queue misconception (claiming queue is LIFO) is caught."""
+    q = questions["queue_001"]
+    answer = "A queue operates on Last In, First Out (LIFO). You enqueue at the front and dequeue at the same end."
+    result = evaluate_answer(q, answer)
+
+    assert len(result["misconceptions"]) > 0
+    assert result["score"] <= 4
+    assert result["recommended_action"] == "scaffold_hint"
+
+
+def test_score_breakdown_bounds(questions):
+    """Verify all rubric components strictly obey maximum allowed points."""
+    q = questions["stack_002"]
+    answers = [
+        "Peek examines the top without removing it. Popping empty stack causes underflow. Overflow occurs when full.",
+        "Just peek.",
+        "Nothing happens",
+    ]
+    for ans in answers:
+        result = evaluate_answer(q, ans)
+        b = result["score_breakdown"]
+        assert 0 <= b["technical_correctness"] <= 4
+        assert 0 <= b["key_concepts"] <= 3
+        assert 0 <= b["reasoning"] <= 2
+        assert 0 <= b["clarity"] <= 1
+        assert result["score"] == (
+            b["technical_correctness"] + b["key_concepts"] + b["reasoning"] + b["clarity"]
+        )
+
+

+    # Rejects invalid action

+        validate_evaluation_result(bad_action)

+    # Rejects missing key
+    missing_key = dict(valid_sample)
+    del missing_key["feedback"]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="missing required keys"):
+        validate_evaluation_result(missing_key)

+def test_bedrock_fallback_safely_evaluates(questions):

+
+

+    """Verify unknown provider raises ValueError."""
+    q = questions["stack_001"]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Unknown evaluation provider"):
+        evaluate_answer(q, "answer", provider="quantum_ai")

+
+

+
+

+    initializes clean state, and sets status to 'in_progress'.
+    """

+    assert session.session_id.startswith("edu_")

+    assert len(session.demonstrated_concepts) == 0

+    """Verify session can start with a valid custom question ID."""
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="queue_001")
+    assert session.current_question_id == "queue_001"
+    assert session.asked_question_ids == ["queue_001"]

+
+def test_start_session_invalid_id_raises_error(engine):
+    """Verify starting with non-existent question ID raises ValueError."""
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not found in question bank"):

+    """
+    PRD FR-06: Requesting a hint retrieves the hint string,
+    marks hint_requested_for_current=True, and increments hints_used_count.
+    Calling hint multiple times on the same question does not double-count.
+    """
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="stack_001")
+    assert not session.hint_requested_for_current
+    assert session.hints_used_count == 0
+
+    hint1 = engine.request_hint(session)
+    assert len(hint1) > 0
+    assert session.hint_requested_for_current
+    assert session.hints_used_count == 1
+
+    # Calling again on same question should not increment count
+    hint2 = engine.request_hint(session)
+    assert hint2 == hint1
+    assert session.hints_used_count == 1
+
+
+def test_empty_answer_submission(engine):
+    """
+    PRD FR-05: Submitting empty or whitespace answer returns score 0,
+    does not advance question, and does not record a completed attempt.
+    """
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="stack_001")
+    eval_res, decision, is_done = engine.submit_answer(session, "   ")
+
+    assert eval_res["score"] == 0
+    assert not is_done
+    assert session.current_question_id == "stack_001"
+    assert len(session.attempts) == 0
+    assert "Write an answer" in eval_res["feedback"]
+
+
+def test_duplicate_submission_protection(engine):
+    """
+    PRD FR-05, TRD Section 15: Rapid duplicate clicks with the same answer
+    do not register multiple attempts.
+    """
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="stack_001")
+    answer = "A stack is Last In First Out (LIFO). Push adds to the top and pop removes from the top."
+
+    # First submission
+    eval1, dec1, done1 = engine.submit_answer(session, answer)
+    initial_attempts = len(session.attempts)
+    assert initial_attempts == 1
+
+    # Second submission with exact same text immediately after
+    eval2, dec2, done2 = engine.submit_answer(session, answer)
+    assert len(session.attempts) == 1  # Deduplicated!
+    assert eval2["score"] == eval1["score"]
+
+
+def test_valid_submission_progression_and_mastery(engine):
+    """
+    PRD FR-02, FR-11, FR-15: A strong answer advances to the next question,
+    records the attempt, updates demonstrated concepts, and resets hint flag.
+    """
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="stack_001")
+    engine.request_hint(session)
+    assert session.hint_requested_for_current
+
+    answer = (
+        "A stack is a linear data structure following Last In First Out (LIFO). "
+        "The push operation inserts an element onto the top of the stack, "
+        "and pop removes the most recently added element from the top."
+    )
+
+    eval_res, decision, is_done = engine.submit_answer(session, answer)
+
+    assert eval_res["score"] >= 8
+    assert len(session.attempts) == 1
+    assert session.attempts[0]["hint_used"] is True
+    assert session.attempts[0]["question_id"] == "stack_001"
+
+    # Must have advanced to a new question
+    assert session.current_question_id != "stack_001"
+    assert session.current_question_id in session.asked_question_ids
+    # Hint flag reset for the new question
+    assert not session.hint_requested_for_current
+
+    # Demonstrated concepts must be populated
+    assert "LIFO" in session.demonstrated_concepts or "push" in session.demonstrated_concepts
+
+
+def test_score_aggregates(engine):
+    """Verify total_score and average_score calculations."""
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="stack_001")
+
+    # Attempt 1: score 10
+    ans1 = "A stack is Last In First Out (LIFO). Push adds to the top and pop removes from the top."
+    engine.submit_answer(session, ans1)
+
+    # Attempt 2: partial answer
+    ans2 = "It is an operation."
+    engine.submit_answer(session, ans2)
+
+    assert session.total_score > 0
+    assert session.average_score > 0.0
+    assert session.average_score == round(session.total_score / 2, 1)
+
+
+def test_explicit_end_session(engine):
+    """PRD FR-03: Ending a session updates session_status to completed."""
+    session = engine.start_session()
+    assert session.session_status == "in_progress"
+
+    engine.end_session(session)
+    assert session.session_status == "completed"
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="already completed"):
+        engine.submit_answer(session, "Late answer")
+
+
+def test_session_serialization_round_trip(engine):
+    """
+    TRD Section 10: Verify InterviewSession.to_dict() and from_dict()
+    perform a flawless round-trip conversion for Streamlit session state.
+    """
+    session = engine.start_session(first_question_id="stack_001")
+    engine.request_hint(session)
+    answer = "A stack is LIFO. Push puts on top and pop takes off top."
+    engine.submit_answer(session, answer)
+
+    data = session.to_dict()
+    assert isinstance(data, dict)
+    assert isinstance(data["demonstrated_concepts"], list)
+    assert isinstance(data["unresolved_concepts"], list)
+
+    restored = InterviewSession.from_dict(data)
+    assert restored.session_id == session.session_id
+    assert restored.current_question_id == session.current_question_id
+    assert restored.session_status == session.session_status
+    assert restored.hints_used_count == session.hints_used_count
+    assert len(restored.attempts) == len(session.attempts)
+    assert restored.demonstrated_concepts == session.demonstrated_concepts
+    assert restored.unresolved_concepts == session.unresolved_concepts
+    assert restored.total_score == session.total_score

+"""
+Unit tests for the Alexa+ Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
+=============================================================
+
+Tests:
+- Server initialization & question bank loading
+- Individual tool execution:
+  - `get_interview_question` (by ID, topic/difficulty filter, error cases)
+  - `evaluate_student_answer` (strong answer, misconception, attempt recording)
+  - `get_session_weaknesses` (tracks session gaps)
+  - `generate_revision_report` (structured report & markdown generation)
+- JSON-RPC 2.0 Protocol Compliance:
+  - `initialize` handshake
+  - `tools/list` schema registry
+  - `tools/call` execution and structured text content output
+  - `tools/call` error handling (returns isError: True)
+  - Unknown method handling (-32601)
+  - Ping and notification handling
+"""
+
+import json
+import pytest
+
+from mcp_server import MCPServer, TOOLS_REGISTRY, MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION, SERVER_NAME
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def mcp():
+    """Fixture providing a fresh MCPServer instance for each test."""
+    server = MCPServer(question_bank_path="question_bank.json")
+    server.reset_session("stack_001")
+    return server
+
+
+# =============================================================================
+# Direct Tool Handler Tests
+# =============================================================================
+
+def test_server_initialization(mcp):
+    assert len(mcp.question_bank) == 10
+    assert mcp.session.session_id is not None
+    assert mcp.session.current_question_id == "stack_001"
+    assert len(mcp.session.attempts) == 0
+
+
+def test_tool_get_interview_question_by_id(mcp):
+    res = mcp.tool_get_interview_question(question_id="stack_001")
+    assert res["id"] == "stack_001"
+    assert res["topic"] == "Stacks"
+    assert res["difficulty"] == "easy"
+    assert "question" in res
+    assert "hint" in res
+    # Ensure internal scoring criteria are NOT exposed to candidate
+    assert "expected_points" not in res
+    assert "critical_misconceptions" not in res
+
+
+def test_tool_get_interview_question_by_filters(mcp):
+    res = mcp.tool_get_interview_question(topic="Queues", difficulty="easy")
+    assert res["topic"] == "Queues"
+    assert res["difficulty"] == "easy"
+    assert res["id"] in ("queue_001", "queue_002")
+
+
+def test_tool_get_interview_question_invalid_id_raises(mcp):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not found in question bank"):
+        mcp.tool_get_interview_question(question_id="non_existent_id")
+
+
+def test_tool_get_interview_question_no_match_raises(mcp):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No questions matched filter"):
+        mcp.tool_get_interview_question(topic="BinaryTrees", difficulty="hard")
+
+
+def test_tool_evaluate_student_answer_strong(mcp):
+    answer = (
+        "A stack is a Last In First Out (LIFO) data structure. "
+        "The push operation adds an element to the top, and the pop operation removes the top element."
+    )
+    result = mcp.tool_evaluate_student_answer(question_id="stack_001", student_answer=answer)
+
+    assert result["score"] >= 8
+    assert result["recommended_action"] == "progress"
+    assert len(result["correct_points"]) >= 3
+
+    # Verify session state was recorded
+    assert len(mcp.session.attempts) == 1
+    assert "stack_001" in mcp.session.asked_question_ids
+    assert len(mcp.session.demonstrated_concepts) > 0
+
+
+def test_tool_evaluate_student_answer_misconception(mcp):
+    answer = "A stack is First In First Out (FIFO). You add to the rear and remove from front."
+    result = mcp.tool_evaluate_student_answer(question_id="stack_001", student_answer=answer)
+
+    assert result["score"] <= 4
+    assert result["recommended_action"] == "scaffold_hint"
+    assert len(result["misconceptions"]) > 0
+
+    # Verify session recorded the gap
+    assert len(mcp.session.unresolved_concepts) > 0
+
+
+def test_tool_evaluate_invalid_question_id_raises(mcp):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not found in question bank"):
+        mcp.tool_evaluate_student_answer("invalid_id", "Some answer")
+
+
+def test_tool_get_session_weaknesses(mcp):
+    # First, submit a misconception answer
+    mcp.tool_evaluate_student_answer(
+        question_id="stack_001",
+        student_answer="A stack is FIFO, like a regular queue.",
+    )
+
+    weaknesses = mcp.tool_get_session_weaknesses()
+    assert weaknesses["session_id"] == mcp.session.session_id
+    assert weaknesses["total_attempts"] == 1
+    assert len(weaknesses["misconceptions_detected"]) > 0
+    assert len(weaknesses["unresolved_concepts"]) > 0
+
+
+def test_tool_generate_revision_report(mcp):
+    # Submit one strong answer and one partial answer
+    mcp.tool_evaluate_student_answer(
+        question_id="stack_001",
+        student_answer="Stack is LIFO. Push inserts at top. Pop deletes from top.",
+    )
+    mcp.tool_evaluate_student_answer(
+        question_id="queue_001",
+        student_answer="A queue adds elements to the back.",
+    )
+
+    report = mcp.tool_generate_revision_report()
+    assert "total_score" in report
+    assert "percentage" in report
+    assert "performance_tier" in report
+    assert "demonstrated_concepts" in report
+    assert "recommendations" in report
+    assert "markdown_report" in report
+    assert report["attempts_count"] == 2
+    assert report["performance_tier"] in ("Proficient", "Developing", "Foundational")
+
+
+# =============================================================================
+# JSON-RPC 2.0 Protocol Compliance Tests
+# =============================================================================
+
+def test_jsonrpc_initialize(mcp):
+    req = {
+        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
+        "id": "req-1",
+        "method": "initialize",
+        "params": {
+            "protocolVersion": MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
+            "capabilities": {},
+            "clientInfo": {"name": "alexa-test-client", "version": "1.0"},
+        },
+    }
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["jsonrpc"] == "2.0"
+    assert resp["id"] == "req-1"
+    assert "result" in resp
+    assert resp["result"]["protocolVersion"] == MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION
+    assert resp["result"]["serverInfo"]["name"] == SERVER_NAME
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_ping(mcp):
+    req = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 100, "method": "ping"}
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == 100
+    assert resp["result"] == {}
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_notifications_return_none(mcp):
+    req = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp is None
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_tools_list(mcp):
+    req = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "list-1", "method": "tools/list"}
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == "list-1"
+    tools = resp["result"]["tools"]
+    assert len(tools) == 4
+    tool_names = [t["name"] for t in tools]
+    assert "get_interview_question" in tool_names
+    assert "evaluate_student_answer" in tool_names
+    assert "get_session_weaknesses" in tool_names
+    assert "generate_revision_report" in tool_names
+
+    # Check inputSchema validity
+    for t in tools:
+        assert "name" in t
+        assert "description" in t
+        assert "inputSchema" in t
+        assert t["inputSchema"]["type"] == "object"
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_tools_call_get_interview_question(mcp):
+    req = {
+        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
+        "id": "call-1",
+        "method": "tools/call",
+        "params": {
+            "name": "get_interview_question",
+            "arguments": {"question_id": "queue_001"},
+        },
+    }
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == "call-1"
+    assert resp["result"]["isError"] is False
+    content_text = resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"]
+    q_data = json.loads(content_text)
+    assert q_data["id"] == "queue_001"
+    assert q_data["topic"] == "Queues"
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_tools_call_evaluate_student_answer(mcp):
+    req = {
+        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
+        "id": "call-2",
+        "method": "tools/call",
+        "params": {
+            "name": "evaluate_student_answer",
+            "arguments": {
+                "question_id": "queue_001",
+                "student_answer": (
+                    "A queue is a First In First Out (FIFO) data structure. "
+                    "Enqueue adds to the rear and dequeue removes from the front."
+                ),
+            },
+        },
+    }
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == "call-2"
+    assert resp["result"]["isError"] is False
+    content_text = resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"]
+    eval_data = json.loads(content_text)
+    assert eval_data["score"] >= 8
+    assert eval_data["recommended_action"] == "progress"
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_tools_call_validation_error(mcp):
+    req = {
+        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
+        "id": "call-err",
+        "method": "tools/call",
+        "params": {
+            "name": "get_interview_question",
+            "arguments": {"question_id": "fake_id_123"},
+        },
+    }
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == "call-err"
+    # In MCP, tool application errors are returned as result with isError=True
+    assert resp["result"]["isError"] is True
+    assert "Validation Error" in resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"]
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_unknown_tool_error(mcp):
+    req = {
+        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
+        "id": "unknown-tool",
+        "method": "tools/call",
+        "params": {
+            "name": "unsupported_tool",
+            "arguments": {},
+        },
+    }
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == "unknown-tool"
+    assert "error" in resp
+    assert resp["error"]["code"] == -32601
+
+
+def test_jsonrpc_unknown_method(mcp):
+    req = {
+        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
+        "id": 999,
+        "method": "non_existent_method",
+    }
+    resp = mcp.dispatch(req)
+    assert resp["id"] == 999
+    assert "error" in resp
+    assert resp["error"]["code"] == -32601
+    assert "Method not found" in resp["error"]["message"]

+import json
+import copy
+from pathlib import Path
+import pytest
+
+QUESTION_BANK_PATH = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "question_bank.json"
+
+REQUIRED_FIELDS = {
+    "id": str,
+    "topic": str,
+    "concepts": list,
+    "difficulty": str,
+    "question": str,
+    "expected_points": list,
+    "critical_misconceptions": list,
+    "hint": str,
+    "follow_up_ids": list,
+    "fallback_follow_up_id": str,
+}
+
+VALID_TOPICS = {"Stacks", "Queues"}
+VALID_DIFFICULTIES = {"easy", "medium", "hard"}
+
+
+def validate_question_bank(questions: list) -> None:
+    """
+    Validates question bank schema and referential integrity per TRD Section 7.4.
+    Raises ValueError on validation failure.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(questions, list):
+        raise ValueError("Question bank must be a list of question objects.")
+
+    if len(questions) == 0:
+        raise ValueError("Question bank cannot be empty.")
+
+    seen_ids = set()
+    for q in questions:
+        if not isinstance(q, dict):
+            raise ValueError(f"Each question must be a dictionary object, got {type(q).__name__}.")
+
+        qid = q.get("id")
+        if not qid or not isinstance(qid, str) or not qid.strip():
+            raise ValueError("Every question must have a non-empty string 'id'.")
+
+        if qid in seen_ids:
+            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate question id found: '{qid}'. IDs must be unique.")
+        seen_ids.add(qid)
+
+        for field, expected_type in REQUIRED_FIELDS.items():
+            if field not in q:
+                raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' is missing required field '{field}'.")
+            if not isinstance(q[field], expected_type):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Question '{qid}' field '{field}' must be {expected_type.__name__}, got {type(q[field]).__name__}."
+                )
+
+        if q["topic"] not in VALID_TOPICS:
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' topic '{q['topic']}' is invalid. Allowed: {VALID_TOPICS}.")
+
+        if q["difficulty"] not in VALID_DIFFICULTIES:
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' difficulty '{q['difficulty']}' is invalid. Allowed: {VALID_DIFFICULTIES}.")
+
+        if len(q["concepts"]) == 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' has an empty 'concepts' list.")
+        if not all(isinstance(c, str) and c.strip() for c in q["concepts"]):
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' concepts must be non-empty strings.")
+
+        if len(q["expected_points"]) == 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' has an empty 'expected_points' list.")
+        if not all(isinstance(p, str) and p.strip() for p in q["expected_points"]):
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' expected points must be non-empty strings.")
+
+        if not isinstance(q["hint"], str) or not q["hint"].strip():
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' must have a non-empty 'hint' string.")
+
+    # Referential integrity check
+    for q in questions:
+        qid = q["id"]
+        for f_id in q["follow_up_ids"]:
+            if f_id not in seen_ids:
+                raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' references nonexistent follow_up_id '{f_id}'.")
+            if f_id == qid:
+                raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' references itself as a follow_up_id (infinite loop).")
+
+        fallback_id = q["fallback_follow_up_id"]
+        if fallback_id not in seen_ids:
+            raise ValueError(f"Question '{qid}' references nonexistent fallback_follow_up_id '{fallback_id}'.")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def questions():
+    """Load question bank JSON file."""
+    assert QUESTION_BANK_PATH.exists(), f"Missing question bank at {QUESTION_BANK_PATH}"
+    with open(QUESTION_BANK_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        data = json.load(f)
+    return data
+
+
+def test_real_question_bank_passes_validation(questions):
+    """Verify that the actual question_bank.json passes all schema and integrity checks."""
+    validate_question_bank(questions)
+
+
+def test_question_count(questions):
+    """Verify question bank contains at least 8 and up to 12 questions as specified in TRD."""
+    assert 8 <= len(questions) <= 12, f"Expected 8-12 questions, found {len(questions)}"
+
+
+def test_topic_distribution(questions):
+    """Verify balanced distribution between Stacks and Queues."""
+    stacks = [q for q in questions if q["topic"] == "Stacks"]
+    queues = [q for q in questions if q["topic"] == "Queues"]
+
+    assert len(stacks) >= 4, f"Expected at least 4 Stacks questions, got {len(stacks)}"
+    assert len(queues) >= 4, f"Expected at least 4 Queues questions, got {len(queues)}"
+
+
+def test_validation_rejects_duplicate_ids(questions):
+    """Verify that questions with duplicate IDs raise ValueError."""
+    bad_questions = copy.deepcopy(questions)
+    bad_questions[1]["id"] = bad_questions[0]["id"]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Duplicate question id"):
+        validate_question_bank(bad_questions)
+
+
+def test_validation_rejects_missing_field(questions):
+    """Verify that questions with a missing required field raise ValueError."""
+    bad_questions = copy.deepcopy(questions)
+    del bad_questions[0]["expected_points"]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="missing required field 'expected_points'"):
+        validate_question_bank(bad_questions)
+
+
+def test_validation_rejects_invalid_follow_up_id(questions):
+    """Verify that questions referencing a nonexistent follow_up_id raise ValueError."""
+    bad_questions = copy.deepcopy(questions)
+    bad_questions[0]["follow_up_ids"].append("nonexistent_id_999")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="references nonexistent follow_up_id"):
+        validate_question_bank(bad_questions)
+
+
+def test_validation_rejects_self_referential_loop(questions):
+    """Verify that a question referencing itself as a follow-up raises ValueError."""
+    bad_questions = copy.deepcopy(questions)
+    bad_questions[0]["follow_up_ids"].append(bad_questions[0]["id"])
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="references itself as a follow_up_id"):
+        validate_question_bank(bad_questions)
+
+
+def test_validation_rejects_invalid_difficulty(questions):
+    """Verify that an invalid difficulty label raises ValueError."""
+    bad_questions = copy.deepcopy(questions)
+    bad_questions[0]["difficulty"] = "insane"
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="difficulty 'insane' is invalid"):
+        validate_question_bank(bad_questions)

+"""
+Automated Unit Tests for Final Report Generator (report_generator.py).
+Verifies report schema completeness, tier calculations, recommendation logic,
+and markdown rendering per PRD FR-16 and TRD Section 13.1.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from interview_engine import InterviewEngine, InterviewSession
+from report_generator import ReportGenerator
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def engine():
+    return InterviewEngine()
+
+
+def test_report_schema_completeness(engine):
+    """
+    PRD FR-16: Verify that all required fields are present in the generated report.
+    """
+    session = engine.start_session()
+    ans = "A stack is a Last In First Out (LIFO) structure. Push adds to top and pop removes from top."
+    engine.submit_answer(session, ans)
+
+    report = ReportGenerator.generate_report(session)
+
+    required_fields = [
+        "session_id",
+        "created_at",
+        "evaluation_mode",
+        "attempts_count",
+        "total_score",

+# EduAgent Interview Coach
+## Product Requirements Document (PRD)
+
+**Document version:** 1.0  
+**Date:** 21 October 2026  
+**Status:** Product baseline  
+**Document type:** Product Requirements Document  
+**Related document:** `EduAgent_Interview_Coach_TRD.md`
+
+---
+
+## 1. Executive Summary
+
+EduAgent Interview Coach is an adaptive, text-based interview practice application designed to help students prepare for technical interviews and viva examinations.
+
+The initial version focuses exclusively on Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA), specifically **Stacks and Queues**, for a Junior Software Developer interview scenario.
+
+Unlike a static question-and-answer practice tool, EduAgent aims to identify gaps in a student's understanding, provide actionable feedback, select targeted follow-up questions, and reassess weak concepts throughout a session.
+
+The product will prioritize educational value, predictable behavior, transparent feedback, and a complete working demonstration over unnecessary features.
+
+The first release will be a focused prototype suitable for a hackathon demonstration. It will not attempt to replace a human interviewer, provide a complete DSA curriculum, or guarantee interview success.
+
+## 2. Problem Statement
+
+Students frequently prepare for technical interviews and university viva examinations by reading notes, watching tutorials, memorizing answers, or solving predetermined questions.
+
+These approaches can help students learn concepts, but they do not always reveal whether a student can explain a concept independently, identify mistakes in their reasoning, or respond to a follow-up question.
+
+Many basic practice tools present a fixed set of questions and answers. They may tell students whether an answer is correct without identifying the specific concepts that are missing or adapting subsequent questions to the student's demonstrated understanding.
+
+This creates several problems:
+
+1. **Limited personalization:** Students with different levels of understanding receive similar practice questions.
+2. **Unclear weaknesses:** Students may know that an answer is incomplete without understanding which concept they missed.
+3. **Insufficient follow-up practice:** A weak answer may not lead to focused practice on the underlying misconception.
+4. **Passive learning:** Reading model answers does not necessarily test the student's ability to explain a concept independently.
+5. **Poor progress visibility:** Students may finish a practice session without a clear summary of demonstrated knowledge and remaining gaps.
+6. **Inconsistent feedback:** Students may struggle to evaluate their own answers against the important concepts expected in a technical interview.
+
+EduAgent Interview Coach addresses these problems by creating a structured practice session in which each submitted answer influences the next learning step.
+
+### 2.1 Product opportunity
+
+A focused interview coach can make practice more useful by combining structured questions, consistent evaluation criteria, targeted follow-ups, and an understandable progress report.
+
+The product's primary differentiator is not merely generating questions or assigning scores. It is the **closed-loop learning process: assess, identify a gap, practice the gap, and reassess**.
+
+## 3. Product Vision
+
+Help students practice explaining technical concepts, understand their mistakes, and improve their interview readiness through personalized, feedback-driven practice.
+
+## 4. Product Goals
+
+### 4.1 Primary goals
+
+- Deliver a complete text-based technical interview simulation.
+- Assess students' written explanations against explicit evaluation criteria.
+- Identify missing concepts and potential misconceptions.
+- Adapt follow-up questions to the student's demonstrated understanding.
+- Help students understand why their answers received particular feedback.
+- Track progress across the current interview session.
+- Produce an actionable final report.
+- Keep the core experience available when external AI services are unavailable.
+
+### 4.2 Secondary goals
+
+- Demonstrate a practical educational use case for AI-assisted evaluation.
+- Show how adaptive questioning can improve upon static practice.
+- Provide a clear foundation for expanding to other DSA topics in a future version.
+- Demonstrate any actual cloud or agent-tool integration required by the hackathon, if implemented and verified.
+
+## 5. Non-Goals
+
+The first release will not attempt to:
+
+- Cover every DSA topic.
+- Support multiple job roles or academic subjects.
+- Conduct voice-based or video-based interviews.
+- Analyze resumes or generate personalized career plans.
+- Execute arbitrary programming submissions or evaluate coding challenges in a sandbox.
+- Replace teachers, mentors, professional interviewers, or formal examinations.
+- Guarantee placement, employment, or examination results.
+- Provide a permanent student profile, social network, or multi-user learning management system.
+- Claim that a simulated tool action is an actual external tool call.
+- Claim that AI-generated scores are objectively accurate or professionally validated.
+
+These exclusions protect the project's focus and make the first release achievable.
+
+## 6. Target Users
+
+### 6.1 Primary user: Student preparing for technical interviews
+
+A student who understands some programming fundamentals but needs practice explaining concepts, answering follow-up questions, and identifying knowledge gaps.
+
+**Needs:**
+- Questions appropriate to their current level.
+- Clear feedback instead of a score alone.
+- Practice on concepts they have not understood.
+- A simple way to review progress.
+
+### 6.2 Secondary user: Student preparing for a viva
+
+A student who wants to practice explaining data structures and their operations before an academic viva or oral assessment.
+
+**Needs:**
+- Conceptual questions.
+- Explanations of missing ideas.
+- Follow-up questions that probe understanding.
+- A summary of topics requiring revision.
+
+### 6.3 Demonstration evaluator
+
+A hackathon judge, mentor, or reviewer assessing the usefulness, reliability, and completeness of the prototype.
+
+**Needs:**
+- A working end-to-end demonstration.
+- Visible evidence of adaptive behavior.
+- Understandable evaluation criteria.
+- Clear differentiation between implemented, simulated, and unavailable functionality.
+
+## 7. Product Scope
+
+### 7.1 Initial release
+
+| Product area | Scope |
+|---|---|
+| Interview role | Junior Software Developer |
+| Subject | Data Structures and Algorithms |
+| Topics | Stacks and Queues |
+| Interaction | Text-only |
+| Question source | Reviewed question set |
+| Evaluation | Consistent ten-point rubric |
+| Adaptation | Concept-based follow-up selection |
+| Feedback | Correct points, missing concepts, misconceptions, and advice |
+| Progress | Current-session tracking |
+| Final output | Interview performance report |
+| Offline behavior | Core practice using local evaluation and Streamlit web interface |
+| Hackathon track integration | Alexa+ MCP Agent Skill (Model Context Protocol server) |
+
+### 7.2 Topic coverage
+
+The question set should cover the following concepts as appropriate to the selected questions:
+
+**Stacks**
+- Last In, First Out (LIFO).
+- Push and pop operations.
+- Peek or top operation.
+- Empty-stack conditions and underflow.
+- Common applications of stacks.
+- Basic time complexity of stack operations.
+
+**Queues**
+- First In, First Out (FIFO).
+- Enqueue and dequeue operations.
+- Front and rear.
+- Empty-queue conditions and underflow.
+- Circular queue fundamentals.
+- Common applications and basic operation complexity.
+
+The first release does not need to test every listed concept in every session. The question bank must provide sufficient coverage to demonstrate meaningful adaptation.
+
+## 8. Core User Journey
+
+1. The student opens the application.
+2. The student sees the interview topic, role, and session instructions.
+3. The student starts a practice interview.
+4. The application presents a question.
+5. The student types and submits an answer.
+6. The application evaluates the answer and presents feedback.
+7. The application identifies a suitable next question based on the evaluation.
+8. The student answers a targeted follow-up or progresses to a more challenging question.
+9. The process continues until the session's completion condition is reached.
+10. The student receives a final report containing performance, demonstrated concepts, unresolved weaknesses, and recommendations.
+
+The experience should feel like a guided technical interview rather than a static quiz.
+
+## 9. Feature Requirements
+
+Priority definitions:
+
+- **P0 — Must have:** Essential for a valid first release.
+- **P1 — Should have:** Important improvement after the core experience works.
+- **P2 — Could have:** Optional enhancement that must not delay the core release.
+
+### 9.1 Start and session management
+
+**FR-01 — Start interview (P0)**
+
+The application shall allow the student to start a new interview session.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The role and topic are visible before starting.
+- A new session begins with a valid question.
+- The application initializes progress tracking.
+- The student receives clear instructions for answering questions.
+
+**FR-02 — Track session progress (P0)**
+
+The application shall track attempted questions, previous evaluations, demonstrated concepts, and unresolved concepts during the active session.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Each accepted submission is recorded once.
+- Progress updates after evaluation.
+- The student can see progress through the interview.
+- A new session starts with a clean state.
+
+**FR-03 — Complete an interview (P0)**
+
+The application shall end a session when its defined stopping condition is met.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The application does not continue indefinitely.
+- The student receives a completion message.
+- The final report is available after completion.
+
+### 9.2 Question presentation and answering
+
+**FR-04 — Present relevant questions (P0)**
+
+The application shall present questions from the approved Stacks and Queues question set.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Each question has a unique identity.
+- Questions have defined concepts and expected answer points.
+- The displayed question matches its stored content.
+- Invalid or missing question data does not silently produce fabricated questions.
+
+**FR-05 — Accept written answers (P0)**
+
+The student shall be able to type and submit an answer.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Empty submissions are handled clearly.
+- Valid submissions are evaluated.
+- Repeated clicks do not create duplicate attempts.
+- The student's input is preserved appropriately during normal interface updates.
+
+**FR-06 — Provide hints (P0)**
+
+The student shall be able to request a hint for the current question.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The hint relates to the current question.
+- The hint helps the student reason about the concept.
+- The hint does not unexpectedly change the current question.
+- Hint usage can be tracked for session feedback if included in the scoring policy.
+
+### 9.3 Answer evaluation
+
+**FR-07 — Evaluate answers consistently (P0)**
+
+The application shall evaluate answers using the defined ten-point rubric.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Each completed evaluation produces a score from 0 to 10.
+- Evaluation feedback uses the same rubric throughout the session.
+- The result identifies relevant correct points and missing concepts.
+- Evaluation output is checked for validity before being shown.
+- The score is described as practice feedback rather than a guaranteed measure of interview ability.
+
+**FR-08 — Identify missing concepts (P0)**
+
+The application shall identify essential concepts that the student's answer does not adequately address.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Missing concepts relate to the current question.
+- Feedback is understandable to a beginner.
+- The application distinguishes missing information from an explicitly incorrect claim when possible.
+- The identified gap can influence the next question.
+
+**FR-09 — Identify possible misconceptions (P0)**
+
+The application shall identify important incorrect claims when supported by the evaluation.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Feedback identifies the concept involved.
+- The student receives a useful correction or explanation.
+- Unsupported claims about the student's understanding are avoided.
+- A critical misconception can trigger a simpler follow-up question.
+
+**FR-10 — Explain feedback (P0)**
+
+The application shall provide actionable feedback rather than a score alone.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The feedback acknowledges important correct elements.
+- It identifies the most important gap.
+- It gives a concrete suggestion for improvement.
+- It does not use unnecessarily harsh or discouraging language.
+
+### 9.4 Adaptive questioning
+
+**FR-11 — Adapt to strong answers (P0)**
+
+The application shall progress to an appropriate next concept or more challenging question when an answer demonstrates sufficient understanding.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The progression follows the predefined adaptation rules.
+- A critical misconception prevents automatic mastery classification.
+- The next question is relevant to the session.
+
+**FR-12 — Target incomplete answers (P0)**
+
+The application shall select a follow-up question related to a missing essential concept when an answer is incomplete.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The follow-up targets an identified gap.
+- The feedback explains why further practice is useful.
+- The application avoids repeating the exact same question unnecessarily.
+
+**FR-13 — Support weak answers (P0)**
+
+The application shall provide a hint and a simpler follow-up when the answer shows substantial misunderstanding.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The follow-up targets a foundational concept.
+- The student receives guidance without being told that improvement is impossible.
+- The session can continue safely after a weak answer.
+
+**FR-14 — Avoid repetitive or invalid question selection (P0)**
+
+The application shall prevent invalid question references and avoid unnecessary repetition.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Only valid questions can be selected.
+- The application handles exhausted follow-up options.
+- Cyclic follow-up relationships cannot create an infinite loop.
+- The interview ends or chooses a valid alternative when no suitable follow-up remains.
+
+**FR-15 — Track concept mastery (P0)**
+
+The application shall maintain a session-level record of concepts that appear demonstrated and concepts that still require practice.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- Mastery status is based on the defined evaluation rules.
+- Missing concepts remain visible until appropriately reassessed.
+- The report distinguishes demonstrated concepts from unresolved ones.
+- The application does not claim mastery based on a single high score when the evaluation identifies a critical misconception.
+
+### 9.5 Final report
+
+**FR-16 — Generate a final report (P0)**
+
+The application shall summarize the completed interview.
+
+**The report must contain:**
+- Overall score or clearly defined aggregate performance.
+- Number of questions attempted.
+- Demonstrated concepts.
+- Concepts requiring further practice.
+- Important misconceptions, if any.
+- Actionable recommendations.
+- Evaluation mode used.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The report reflects the actual session data.
+- Unassessed concepts are not falsely marked as mastered.
+- Recommendations relate to observed gaps.
+- Any limitations of the evaluation are communicated appropriately.
+
+### 9.6 Evaluation service and reliability
+
+**FR-17 — Support local evaluation (P0)**
+
+The core interview experience shall work without an external AI service.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- A complete session can run in local mode.
+- The application does not require cloud credentials to start local practice.
+- Local evaluation is clearly identified.
+- Known limitations of rule-based assessment are not hidden.
+
+**FR-18 — Support Alexa+ MCP Agent Skill (P0 / Primary Hackathon Track)**
+
+The application shall provide a self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes EduAgent Interview Coach capabilities to Alexa+ agents, supporting the "Build, Ship, Shape" Amazon Developer Hackathon (Track: Alexa+ MCP Agent Skills).
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- The application exposes standardized MCP tools: `get_interview_question`, `evaluate_student_answer`, `get_session_weaknesses`, and `generate_revision_report`.
+- Each tool strictly validates its input arguments against defined schemas.
+- The MCP server operates reliably over stdio or SSE transport.
+- The Alexa+ agent skill can conduct an interview, query candidate weak spots, and trigger revision reports.
+- Offline-first operation is maintained: the core Streamlit app and local evaluator function independently of external MCP client connections.
+
+**FR-19 — Recover from evaluation failure (P0)**
+
+The application shall handle invalid model responses, unavailable services, and missing configuration.
+
+**Acceptance criteria:**
+- A useful error or fallback status is displayed.
+- The application does not present malformed output as a valid score.
+- The session remains usable when local evaluation is available.
+- Retry behavior is bounded.
+
+### 9.7 Transparency and user experience
+
+**FR-20 — Show evaluation mode (P0)**
+
+The application shall distinguish local evaluation from AI-assisted evaluation.
+
+**FR-21 — Explain adaptive decisions (P0)**
+
+The application shall provide a brief explanation of why a follow-up question was selected.
+
+**FR-22 — Maintain a clear interface (P0)**
+
+The application shall provide clear question, answer, feedback, progress, and completion states.
+
+**FR-23 — Disclose external data processing (P0)**
+
+When external evaluation or agent connections are enabled, the application shall explain that the submitted answer and necessary question context may be processed by the connected service.
+
+### 9.8 Optional enhancements
+
+**FR-24 — Agent activity trace (P1)**
+
+The application may show a short activity trace, such as “Answer evaluated,” “Missing concept identified,” and “Follow-up selected.”
+
+The trace must reflect actual application events. Simulated actions must be explicitly labelled as simulated.
+
+**FR-25 — Multi-Modal Alexa+ Voice & Device Extension (P2, Optional)**
+
+The application may extend the MCP server to support multi-modal or voice-driven interactions with Alexa+ devices (such as Echo Show or Fire TV multi-screen pairing).
+
+Any implemented extension must use supported APIs, validate inputs, and report success only after a valid response is verified.
+
+This feature must not delay the core web application or standard MCP server release.
+
+## 10. Evaluation and Adaptation Policy
+
+### 10.1 Scoring rubric
+
+| Criterion | Maximum points |
+|---|---:|
+| Technical correctness | 4 |
+| Key concepts | 3 |
+| Reasoning | 2 |
+| Clarity | 1 |
+| **Total** | **10** |
+
+The rubric should be applied consistently to all relevant questions. Each question should define the essential concepts needed to assess its answer.
+
+### 10.2 Adaptation thresholds
+
+| Result | Interpretation | Next action |
+|---|---|---|
+| 8–10 with no critical misconception | Strong response | Progress to a new concept or harder question |
+| 5–7, or an important missing concept | Partial understanding | Ask a targeted follow-up |
+| 0–4, or a critical misconception | Foundational gap | Offer a hint and a simpler follow-up |
+
+These thresholds are initial product rules, not empirically validated cutoffs. They may be adjusted after testing, provided the behavior remains documented and consistent.
+
+### 10.3 Fairness and limitations
+
+- A correct explanation should receive credit even if the wording differs from the expected answer.
+- A matching keyword must not automatically establish that an answer is correct.
+- The application should distinguish uncertainty from a definite error.
+- The application must not claim human-level evaluation accuracy without evidence.
+- The same answer may receive different evaluations from different AI models; the selected provider and evaluation mode should therefore be disclosed.
+- The local evaluator should favor transparent, limited claims over unsupported semantic judgments.
+
+## 11. User Experience Requirements
+
+### 11.1 Start screen
+
+The start screen must show:
+- Product name and purpose.
+- Interview role.
+- Topic coverage.
+- Instructions for written answers.
+- Evaluation mode.
+- A clear start action.
+
+### 11.2 Interview screen
+
+The interview screen must show:
+- Current question.
+- Topic or difficulty where useful.
+- Answer input.
+- Submit action.
+- Hint action.
+- Progress indicator.
+
+### 11.3 Feedback screen
+
+The feedback view must show:
+- Score out of ten.
+- Correct points.
+- Missing concepts.
+- Possible misconceptions.
+- Actionable feedback.
+- Reason for the next question.
+
+### 11.4 Completion screen
+
+The completion view must show:
+- Final performance summary.
+- Demonstrated and unresolved concepts.
+- Suggested areas for revision.
+- Evaluation-mode disclosure.
+- A way to begin a new session.
+
+### 11.5 Accessibility and usability
+
+- Use readable text and consistent labels.
+- Do not rely on color alone to communicate correctness.
+- Keep feedback concise and actionable.
+- Avoid unnecessary steps between questions.
+- Display loading, error, and completion states clearly.
+
+## 12. Data, Privacy, and Trust Requirements
+
+The first version is a practice prototype and does not require user accounts.
+
+- Session information should be used to provide feedback and produce the current report.
+- The product should not claim permanent storage unless that feature is implemented.
+- External AI processing must be disclosed when enabled.
+- Credentials and sensitive configuration must never appear in the UI or logs.
+- Student answers should not be logged unnecessarily.
+- The report must not imply that practice results guarantee real-world interview performance.
+- Mocked outputs and simulated actions must not be presented as verified external results.
+
+## 13. Success Metrics and Acceptance Targets
+
+Success must be assessed through observable product behavior rather than claims about educational outcomes that have not been measured.
+
+### 13.1 Functional success metrics
+
+| Metric | Initial target |
+|---|---|
+| Complete interview flow | 100% of defined acceptance scenarios pass |
+| Valid question references | 100% of selected question IDs exist in the approved question bank |
+| Score validity | 100% of displayed scores are within 0–10 |
+| Duplicate submissions | No duplicate attempt from a single submission action |
+| Adaptive behavior | All defined adaptation test cases pass |
+| Invalid AI response handling | Every tested malformed response is rejected or safely handled |
+| Local-mode operation | A complete interview works without AWS credentials |
+| Final report completeness | All required report fields are present |
+| Question-bank validation | Invalid IDs and missing required fields are detected before use |
+| Demo reproducibility | A fresh setup can follow the README and run the application |
+
+These targets apply to tested application behavior. They do not imply that every semantic evaluation is correct.
+
+### 13.2 Product-quality metrics
+
+Track the following during development and demonstration:
+
+- **Adaptive relevance:** How often a follow-up targets the gap identified in the previous evaluation.
+- **Feedback usefulness:** Whether testers can identify what to improve after reading the feedback.
+- **Session completion:** Whether testers can finish a session without assistance.
+- **Error recovery:** Whether the application remains usable after an evaluation failure.
+- **Demo reliability:** Whether the prepared demonstration works repeatedly under the documented conditions.
+- **Transparency:** Whether testers can tell which evaluation mode was used and why the next question appeared.
+
+### 13.3 Usability validation
+
+Before submission, ask a small group of testers to complete the interview without step-by-step guidance.
+
+Record:
+- Whether they understand the purpose of the application.
+- Whether they can submit answers and request hints.
+- Whether the feedback is understandable.
+- Whether follow-ups appear relevant.
+- Whether the final report provides useful next steps.
+
+Do not claim user satisfaction, learning improvement, or superior accuracy without actual test evidence.
+
+## 14. Hackathon Demonstration Criteria
+
+The demonstration should establish five things:
+
+1. **A real problem is addressed:** Students need practice that identifies gaps, not merely displays static answers.
+2. **The core experience works:** A complete interview can be started, answered, evaluated, and completed.
+3. **Adaptation is visible:** A missing concept leads to a relevant follow-up, while a strong answer leads to progression.
+4. **The product is trustworthy:** Feedback, scoring limitations, and evaluation mode are clear.
+5. **Claims match the implementation:** Any live Alexa+ MCP feature is demonstrated through an actual successful integration; otherwise, it is labelled optional, unavailable, or simulated.
+
+A successful demonstration should include at least one strong answer, one incomplete answer, and one weak answer or critical misconception to show the different adaptation paths.
+
+## 15. Risks and Mitigations
+
+| Risk | Potential impact | Mitigation |
+|---|---|---|
+| Inaccurate AI evaluation | Misleading student feedback | Reviewed expected points, validation, and transparent limitations |
+| Weak local evaluation | Incorrect treatment of paraphrased answers | Restrict claims, test known examples, and disclose local-mode limitations |
+| Irrelevant follow-up questions | Poor adaptive experience | Explicit follow-up links, concept tags, and acceptance tests |
+| Repetitive questions | Frustrating sessions | Track attempted IDs and define termination rules |
+| External service outage | Interrupted interview | Local fallback and clear status |
+| Unavailable MCP client / environment | Missing agent integration demo | Provide self-hosted MCP server with stdio/SSE inspection and test harness |
+| Excessive scope | Incomplete submission | Prioritize P0 features and defer optional enhancements |
+| Misleading performance claims | Reduced trust | Use measurable acceptance criteria and report only observed results |
+| Privacy concerns | Unnecessary exposure of student answers | Disclose external processing and minimize logging |
+| Unverified hackathon requirements | Ineligible or incomplete submission | Check current official rules and eligibility before finalizing the submission |
+

+
+### 16.1 Product dependencies
+
+- A reviewed question set for Stacks and Queues.
+- A defined evaluation rubric.
+- Explicit adaptation rules.
+- Acceptance tests for the major user journeys.
+- Self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Alexa+ agent integration.

+- The selected submission track accepts the intended implementation.
+- The project can be completed within the remaining development time.
+- Any MCP or other integration requirement is explicitly confirmed rather than inferred.
+
+These assumptions must not be represented as confirmed requirements until verified.
+
