+# EduAgent Interview Coach
+
+## Technology Requirements Document (TRD)
+
+**Document version:** 1.0
+**Date:** 21 October 2026
+**Status:** Initial technical baseline
+**Related document:** `EduAgent_Interview_Coach_PRD.md`
+
+---
+
+## 1. Purpose
+
+This document defines the technical architecture, programming languages, packages, libraries, data formats, interfaces, security measures, testing strategy, and implementation decisions for EduAgent Interview Coach.
+
+It serves as the technical implementation guide for building a working hackathon prototype with a small team or as a solo beginner developer.
+
+### 1.1 Product scope
+
+EduAgent Interview Coach is a text-based interview practice web application. The first version focuses exclusively on **Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA): Stacks and Queues**.
+
+The application asks questions, evaluates typed answers, identifies missing concepts, selects targeted follow-up questions, tracks progress, and generates a final performance report.
+
+### 1.2 Core technical principles
+
+1. Keep the application small and modular.
+2. Make core interview functionality work without an external AI service.
+3. Use explicitly reviewed questions instead of unrestricted question generation.
+4. Keep adaptive question selection deterministic and testable.
+5. Provide a self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Alexa+ Agent Skills.
+6. Support offline-first local evaluation with structured validation.
+7. Do not claim that simulated agent actions are actual external tool calls.
+8. Avoid unnecessary infrastructure, dependencies, and features.
+
+---
+
+## 2. System Requirements
+
+### 2.1 Functional requirements
+
+The system must:
+
+- Start and run a text-only interview session.
+- Present questions from a local question bank.
+- Accept a student's typed answer.
+- Evaluate the answer using a defined scoring rubric.
+- Identify correct points, missing concepts, and possible misconceptions.
+- Choose a follow-up question based on the evaluation.
+- Track attempted questions and demonstrated concepts.
+- Allow the student to request a hint.
+- Generate a final report with scores and recommendations.
+- Work entirely offline without external credentials or network access.
+- Expose standardized MCP tools for Alexa+ Agent Skills.
+- Recover gracefully from malformed inputs or service failures.
+
+### 2.2 Non-functional requirements
+
+| Requirement     | Technical target                                                    |
+| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Reliability     | Core interview loop works without network access after installation |
+| Maintainability | Separate UI, interview flow, evaluation, and adaptation modules     |
+| Testability     | Core logic can be tested without launching Streamlit                |
+| Security        | No API keys committed to source control                             |
+| Explainability  | Show why a follow-up question was selected                          |
+| Performance     | Avoid unnecessary external calls and repeated evaluations           |
+| Portability     | Run on a supported Windows, Linux, or macOS Python environment      |
+| Usability       | Clear question progress, feedback, hints, and completion state      |
+
+---
+
+## 3. Technology Stack
+
+### 3.1 Selected technologies
+
+| Layer                | Technology                                                   | Purpose                                 |
+| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
+| Programming language | Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.14                                   | Main application language               |
+| User interface       | Streamlit                                                    | Interactive web application             |
+| Question storage     | JSON                                                         | Local, version-controlled question bank |
+| Application state    | Streamlit Session State                                      | Current session and progress            |
+| Evaluation           | Python deterministic rules + concept synonym clusters        | Answer assessment                       |
+| Agent Integration    | Model Context Protocol (MCP standard)                        | Alexa+ Agent Skill interface            |
+| Configuration        | Environment variables; `python-dotenv` for local development | Manage configuration and ports          |
+| Validation           | Python standard library                                      | Validate data and tool schemas          |
+| Unit testing         | Pytest                                                       | Test core application behavior          |
+| Version control      | Git                                                          | Track code and configuration changes    |
+| Documentation        | Markdown                                                     | PRD, TRD, README, friction log          |
+
+### 3.2 Explicitly excluded from version 1
+
+The following are not part of the initial implementation:
+
+- React, Next.js, or a separate JavaScript frontend.
+- A separate FastAPI backend (Streamlit + standard MCP server handles both UI and agent access).
+- PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or Redis.
+- User accounts and authentication.
+- Voice recognition, speech synthesis, or live audio.
+- Resume parsing and coding-execution environments.
+- Training or fine-tuning a custom model.
+- Kubernetes, Docker-based orchestration, or microservices.
+- Mandatory cloud hosting.
+
+These exclusions keep the application achievable and reduce the number of failure points during the hackathon.
+
+---
+
+## 4. System Architecture
+
+### 4.1 High-level architecture
+
+```text
+                 STUDENT                        ALEXA+ AGENT
+                    |                                 |
+                    v                                 v
+          +---------------------+           +---------------------+
+          | Streamlit UI        |           | Alexa+ MCP Server   |
+          | app.py              |           | mcp_server.py       |
+          +---------------------+           +---------------------+
+                    |                                 |
+                    +---------------+-----------------+
+                                    |
+                                    v
+                          +---------------------+
+                          | Interview Engine    |
+                          | Session lifecycle   |
+                          +---------------------+
+                                    |
+                          +---------+----------+
+                          |                    |
+                          v                    v
+                +------------------+  +------------------+
+                | Question Bank    |  | Evaluator        |
+                | JSON file        |  | 10-point rubric  |
+                | Reviewed prompts |  | Local Evaluator  |
+                +------------------+  +------------------+
+                          |                    |
+                          |                    v
+                          |          +------------------+
+                          |          | Output Validator |
+                          |          | Schema + ranges  |
+          |          +------------------+
+          |                    |
+          +----------+---------+
+                     |
+                     v
+          +---------------------+
+          | Adaptive Engine     |
+          | Rules + concept map |
+          +---------------------+
+                     |
+                     v
+          +---------------------+
+          | Session Report      |
+          | Scores and feedback |
+          +---------------------+
+```
+
+### 4.2 Architecture explanation
+
+**Streamlit UI:** Displays the interview, collects typed answers, displays feedback, and manages user interactions.
+
+**Interview Engine:** Coordinates the session lifecycle, question presentation, answer submission, evaluation, and completion.
+
+**Question Bank:** Supplies reviewed questions and their concept tags, difficulty, hints, and follow-up relationships.
+
+**Evaluator:** Scores the submitted answer using the local evaluator or the configured AI provider.
+
+**Output Validator:** Checks that an evaluation contains the required fields, valid score ranges, and acceptable values.
+
+**Adaptive Engine:** Applies deterministic rules to select the next question based on the evaluation and previous attempts.
+
+**Session Report:** Summarizes the session's performance, demonstrated concepts, unresolved weaknesses, and recommendations.
+
+### 4.3 Architecture decision: one application, modular files
+
+Use a **modular monolithic architecture**.
+
+Every module runs inside the same Python application. Modules have separate responsibilities, but no network APIs are required between them.
+
+This is preferable to a separate frontend and backend because it reduces deployment complexity, dependency management, and debugging effort.
+

+## 6. Runtime and Package Requirements
+
+### 6.1 Python version
+
+Use Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.14 for implementation and testing.
+
+Select one Python version for development and testing, then use that same version for the final demo. Avoid changing the Python version late in development.

+### 6.2 Required packages

+

+
+## 7. Question Bank Specification
+
+### 7.1 Storage decision
+
+Store reviewed questions in `question_bank.json`.
+
+The question bank must be version-controlled and loadable without a database or internet connection.
+
+### 7.2 Required question fields
+
+Each question should contain:
+
+- `id`: Unique identifier.
+- `topic`: Topic name.
+- `concepts`: Concepts assessed by the question.
+- `difficulty`: `easy`, `medium`, or `hard`.
+- `question`: The prompt shown to the student.
+- `expected_points`: Essential ideas an answer should cover.
+- `critical_misconceptions`: Errors that require additional teaching.
+- `hint`: A short hint.
+- `follow_up_ids`: IDs of appropriate follow-up questions.
+- `fallback_follow_up_id`: A safe default follow-up, if applicable.
+
+### 7.3 Example question
+
+```json
+{
+  "id": "stack_001",
+  "topic": "Stacks",
+  "concepts": ["LIFO", "push", "pop"],
+  "difficulty": "easy",
+  "question": "Explain the LIFO principle of a stack and describe push and pop operations.",
+  "expected_points": [
+    "LIFO means Last In, First Out",
+    "Push adds an element to the top",
+    "Pop removes the top element"
+  ],
+  "critical_misconceptions": [
+    "Pop removes the oldest element"
+  ],
+  "hint": "Think about a stack of plates.",
+  "follow_up_ids": ["stack_002", "stack_003"],
+  "fallback_follow_up_id": "stack_002"
+}
+```
+
+This is a format example; the final question bank must be reviewed and tested before the demo.
+
+### 7.4 Question-bank validation
+
+At application startup:
+
+1. Verify that the file exists and contains valid JSON.
+2. Verify that every question has the required fields.
+3. Verify that IDs are unique.
+4. Verify that referenced follow-up IDs exist.
+5. Verify that difficulty values are allowed.
+6. Verify that concepts and expected points are non-empty.
+7. Display a useful error if validation fails.
+
+Do not silently skip malformed questions or replace a missing question bank with fabricated data.
+
+---
+
+## 8. Evaluation Architecture
+
+### 8.1 Evaluation providers
+
+The evaluator should expose one consistent interface regardless of provider.
+
+```python
+def evaluate_answer(question, answer):
+    ...
+```
+
+It returns a validated evaluation result.
+
+Internally, the application uses:
+
+- `LocalEvaluator`: Deterministic, offline 10-point rubric evaluation using conceptual synonym clusters and misconception detection.
+- Standardized evaluation interface callable directly by the Streamlit UI or externally via the Alexa+ MCP Server (`evaluate_student_answer` tool).
+
+Both invocation paths return the identical validated result structure.
+
+### 8.2 Evaluation result schema
+
+```json
+{
+  "score": 7,
+  "score_breakdown": {
+    "technical_correctness": 3,
+    "key_concepts": 2,
+    "reasoning": 1,
+    "clarity": 1
+  },
+  "correct_points": [
+    "Correctly identified LIFO"
+  ],
+  "missing_concepts": [
+    "Did not explain pop"
+  ],
+  "misconceptions": [],
+  "feedback": "Your definition is correct, but explain both push and pop operations.",
+  "confidence": "high",
+  "recommended_action": "targeted_follow_up",
+  "evaluation_provider": "local"
+}
+```
+
+The schema is enforced by `validate_evaluation_result(result)`. The application validates every field before using the result.
+
+### 8.3 Scoring rubric
+
+Use the PRD's ten-point rubric:
+
+| Criterion             | Maximum score |
+| --------------------- | ------------: |
+| Technical correctness |             4 |
+| Key concepts          |             3 |
+| Reasoning             |             2 |
+| Clarity               |             1 |
+| **Total**             |        **10** |
+
+The final score must be an integer from 0 to 10.
+
+The rubric provides practice feedback, not a validated measure of real interview performance. The application should not imply that its scores are objectively accurate or equivalent to an employer's assessment.
+
+### 8.4 Local evaluator
+
+The local evaluator must:
+
+- Work without credentials or internet access.
+- Use reviewed question metadata, expected concepts, and critical misconceptions.
+- Identify clearly missing essential points and misconceptions.
+- Produce consistent, deterministic results for identical inputs.
+- Avoid claiming semantic understanding it cannot reliably provide.
+
+A local keyword or phrase matcher is an offline assessment tool. It may miss certain paraphrases or nuanced explanations. Communicate this transparently in the interface and final report.
+
+### 8.5 MCP Agent Tool Interface
+
+When invoked by an Alexa+ agent or external client, the evaluation tool receives:
+
+- The question ID or question text.
+- The student's answer.
+- Optional evaluation mode parameter.
+
+It validates the input, runs the evaluator, verifies the output schema, and returns structured JSON conforming to the MCP tool specification.
+
+The external agent must not be allowed to choose arbitrary question IDs or directly alter internal session state without passing through the Interview Engine.
+
+### 8.6 Validation and fallback
+
+Before an evaluation is accepted, validate:
+
+- Required keys are present.
+- `score` is an integer from 0 to 10.
+- Feedback fields have the expected types.
+- `confidence` uses an allowed value.
+- `recommended_action` is one of the supported actions.
+- Text and list sizes are within reasonable limits.
+
+If AI evaluation fails, returns malformed data, times out, or exceeds the configured retry limit:
+
+1. Record a diagnostic event without exposing secrets.
+2. Run the local evaluator if the answer can be evaluated locally.
+3. Clearly indicate that fallback evaluation was used.
+4. Continue the interview if safe.
+5. Never present an unvalidated model response as a trusted result.
+
+---
+
+## 9. Adaptive Engine Specification
+
+### 9.1 Decision ownership
+
+The adaptive engine is deterministic application code. It uses the evaluation result, question metadata, attempted-question history, and demonstrated concepts.
+
+The AI evaluator supplies evidence for the decision, but does not control the decision process.
+
+### 9.2 Decision rules
+
+| Evaluation result                       | Application action                                                        |
+| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Score 8–10, no critical misconception   | Mark applicable concepts as demonstrated and select a next-level question |
+| Score 5–7 or essential concepts missing | Select a targeted follow-up covering the missing concepts                 |
+| Score 0–4 or a critical misconception   | Show a hint and select a simpler scaffolded follow-up                     |
+| No eligible follow-up exists            | Select an appropriate unattempted question or end the session             |
+| Evaluation fails                        | Use the local fallback and apply the same validated decision rules        |
+
+A high score alone must not mark a concept as demonstrated if the evaluation identifies a critical misconception.
+
+### 9.3 Selection constraints
+
+The adaptive engine must:
+
+- Select only IDs that exist in the question bank.
+- Avoid asking the exact same question repeatedly within a session, except when an explicit retry feature is introduced.
+- Prefer questions that target unresolved concepts.
+- Avoid selecting a question already attempted when a suitable alternative exists.
+- Avoid infinite loops if follow-up links form a cycle.
+- Have a defined end condition when no suitable questions remain.
+
+### 9.4 Explainability
+
+For each adaptive decision, keep an internal reason such as:
+
+- `missing_concept`
+- `critical_misconception`
+- `mastery_demonstrated`
+- `fallback_after_evaluation_error`
+- `no_eligible_follow_up`
+
+The UI can translate this into a student-friendly message such as: “Next question selected because your answer did not explain the pop operation.”
+
+---
+
+## 10. Interview Session and State Management
+
+### 10.1 State storage decision
+
+Use `st.session_state` for the active interview session.
+
+Do not introduce a database for the first version.
+
+### 10.2 Suggested session state
+
+```python
+{
+    "session_id": "...",
+    "current_question_id": "stack_001",
+    "attempts": [],
+    "demonstrated_concepts": [],
+    "unresolved_concepts": [],
+    "asked_question_ids": [],
+    "evaluation_provider": "local",
+    "session_status": "in_progress"
+}
+```
+
+This illustrates the logical fields; the implementation may use dataclasses or another simple Python structure.
+
+### 10.3 State rules
+
+- Initialize state only when a new session starts.
+- Preserve state across Streamlit reruns.
+- Record an answer only once per submission.
+- Prevent double-submission from creating duplicate attempts.
+- Reset only when the student explicitly starts a new session.
+- Show a clear completion state when the interview ends.
+
+**Limitation:** Session state is not permanent storage. It may be lost when the browser session or server process is reset. Persistent accounts, history, and cross-device synchronization are outside version 1.
+
+---
+
+## 11. Alexa+ MCP Server Architecture (Model Context Protocol)
+
+### 11.1 Purpose and Hackathon Track Alignment
+
+In alignment with the "Build, Ship, Shape" Amazon Developer Hackathon primary track: **Alexa+ (including Model Context Protocol / MCP Agent Skills)**, EduAgent Interview Coach provides a self-hosted Model Context Protocol server (`mcp_server.py`).
+
+This architecture allows Alexa+ assistants and autonomous agents to conduct technical interview preparation, dynamically evaluate candidate explanations using the locked 10-point rubric, inspect candidate knowledge gaps, and generate revision reports.
+
+### 11.2 MCP Transport and Configuration
+
+The server supports two standard MCP transports:
+- **`stdio` (Standard I/O):** For direct integration with local agent runtimes and command-line MCP clients.
+- **`sse` (Server-Sent Events / HTTP):** For network-based communication with Alexa+ agent skills and developer test harnesses (configured via `MCP_SERVER_HOST` and `MCP_SERVER_PORT`).
+
+Example `.env.example`:
+
+```text
+EVALUATION_MODE=local
+MCP_SERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1
+MCP_SERVER_PORT=8000
+MCP_TRANSPORT=stdio
+```
+
+### 11.3 Exposed MCP Tool Specifications
+
+The MCP server exposes four focused, high-value tools conforming to the official Model Context Protocol JSON schema:
+
+#### Tool 1: `get_interview_question`
+- **Description:** Retrieve an interview question from the reviewed Stacks and Queues question bank.
+- **Input schema:**
+  - `topic` (string, optional): `"Stacks"` or `"Queues"`.
+  - `difficulty` (string, optional): `"easy"`, `"medium"`, or `"hard"`.
+  - `question_id` (string, optional): Specific ID (e.g., `"stack_001"`).
+- **Output:** JSON containing `id`, `topic`, `difficulty`, `question`, and `hint`.
+
+#### Tool 2: `evaluate_student_answer`
+- **Description:** Evaluate a candidate's written technical explanation against the 10-point rubric and identify missing concepts and critical misconceptions.
+- **Input schema:**
+  - `question_id` (string, required): The ID of the question being answered.
+  - `student_answer` (string, required): The candidate's explanation.
+- **Output:** Validated evaluation result containing `score` (0–10), `score_breakdown`, `correct_points`, `missing_concepts`, `misconceptions`, `feedback`, `recommended_action`, and `confidence`.
+
+#### Tool 3: `get_session_weaknesses`
+- **Description:** Retrieve the candidate's tracked concept gaps, unresolved topics, and identified misconceptions from the active interview session.
+- **Input schema:** None.
+- **Output:** List of unresolved concept tags and misconception details.
+
+#### Tool 4: `generate_revision_report`
+- **Description:** Generate a comprehensive post-interview performance report and prioritized study recommendations.
+- **Input schema:** None.
+- **Output:** Complete session report including aggregate score, attempted questions, demonstrated concepts, unresolved gaps, and prioritized study recommendations.
+
+### 11.4 Security and Validation Rules
+
+- **Strict Schema Enforcement:** Every tool argument is validated against its schema before processing.
+- **Sandboxed Execution:** The MCP server strictly exposes domain-specific interview tools; no arbitrary file access, shell execution, or unrestricted networking is permitted.
+- **No Credential Leakage:** Sensitive environment variables or system paths are never exposed in tool outputs or error messages.
+
+---
+
+## 12. Offline-First Design and Agent Transparency
+
+### 12.1 Offline-First Principle
+
+EduAgent is built offline-first:
+- The Streamlit web interface (`app.py`), question bank (`question_bank.json`), and evaluation engine (`evaluator.py`) operate without any external network dependency.
+- The Alexa+ MCP Server uses the same core domain logic, ensuring that agent capabilities are 100% testable and operable locally.
+
+### 12.2 Transparency and Truthfulness
+
+- **Never fake tool execution:** When testing or demonstrating the MCP integration, calls must execute real functions against the question bank and evaluator.
+- **Clear Mode Indicators:** The UI and report generator clearly display the active operational mode (`"local"`).
+- **Explainable Decisions:** Every adaptive recommendation provides a beginner-friendly explanation explaining why the action was chosen.
+
+---
+
+## 13. User Interface Requirements
+
+### 13.1 Required screens
+
+**A. Start screen**
+
+- Product title and purpose.
+- Topic and role: DSA — Stacks and Queues; Junior Software Developer.
+- Evaluation mode indicator.
+- Start interview button.
+
+**B. Interview screen**
+
+- Current question and difficulty.
+- Progress indicator.
+- Text input for the answer.
+- Submit answer and hint controls.
+- Clear submission and loading states.
+
+**C. Feedback screen**
+
+- Score out of 10.
+- Correct points.
+- Missing concepts.
+- Possible misconceptions.
+- Actionable feedback.
+- Explanation of the next-question choice.
+
+**D. Final report**
+
+- Overall score and number of attempts.
+- Demonstrated concepts.
+- Concepts that need more practice.
+- Recommended next steps.
+- Evaluation-mode disclosure and relevant limitations.
+
+### 13.2 UI behavior
+
+- Keep navigation simple.
+- Preserve typed answers appropriately during reruns.
+- Disable repeated submissions while evaluation is in progress.
+- Show a clear error message when a question cannot be loaded.
+- Make hints optional and accessible.
+- Do not display raw secrets, internal credentials, or unnecessary stack traces.
+- Label simulated agent actions as simulated.
+
+---
+
+## 14. Data Handling and Privacy
+
+### 14.1 Initial data policy
+
+Version 1 does not require user accounts or a central database. Session data is held in application memory.
+
+### 14.2 External evaluation disclosure
+
+If Bedrock is enabled, the student's answer and necessary question context are sent to the configured AWS service for evaluation.
+
+The interface and README should explain this behavior and identify the local evaluation option.
+
+### 14.3 Logging policy
+
+Logs may contain:
+
+- Timestamp.
+- Event type.
+- Evaluation provider.
+- Success or failure status.
+- Error category.
+- Latency measurement, if implemented.
+
+Do not log:
+
+- AWS secrets or access tokens.
+- Environment-variable dumps.
+- Full credentials or authorization headers.
+- Student answers by default.
+
+If diagnostic answer logging is temporarily required, make it explicit, minimize the data, and remove it from the final default configuration.
+
+---
+
+## 15. Error Handling
+
+| Failure                      | Required behavior                                           |
+| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Question bank missing        | Display a clear startup error                               |
+| Invalid question JSON        | Stop unsafe question loading and report the problem         |
+| Invalid follow-up reference  | Fail validation before the session starts                   |
+| Empty answer                 | Request an answer or provide guidance                       |
+| MCP client disconnect        | Gracefully close connection without stopping server         |
+| Invalid MCP tool arguments   | Return structured JSON-RPC error schema                     |
+| Invalid evaluation result    | Reject it and flag schema failure                           |
+| Duplicate submission         | Avoid creating a duplicate attempt                          |
+| No eligible follow-up        | Select a valid remaining question or finish                 |
+| Session state missing        | Offer a safe restart                                        |
+| Unexpected application error | Show a concise user-facing message and log safe diagnostics |
+
+Errors must not cause an infinite loop or silently create unsupported scores.
+
+---
+
+## 16. Testing Strategy
+
+### 16.1 Unit tests
+
+**Question bank tests**
+
+- Valid file loads.
+- Duplicate IDs are rejected.
+- Missing fields are rejected.
+- Invalid follow-up IDs are rejected.
+
+**Evaluator tests**
+
+- Scores remain within 0–10.
+- Required result fields are present.
+- Malformed evaluation results are rejected.
+- Local evaluation works offline without credentials.
+- Critical misconceptions cap score and recommend hint scaffolding.
+
+**Adaptive engine tests**
+
+- Strong answers move to appropriate questions.
+- Missing concepts trigger targeted follow-ups.
+- Weak answers trigger scaffolded follow-ups.
+- Repeated-question loops are prevented.
+- The engine handles an exhausted question bank.
+
+**Interview engine tests**
+
+- A session starts correctly.
+- An answer is recorded once.
+- A validated evaluation updates progress.
+- The session ends when no valid questions remain.
+- Multiple submissions are deduplicated.
+
+### 16.2 Integration tests
+
+- Run the full interview with local evaluation.
+- Run the interface with valid and invalid question-bank data.
+- Test Alexa+ MCP server tools (`get_interview_question`, `evaluate_student_answer`, `get_session_weaknesses`, `generate_revision_report`) over stdio transport.
+
+Automated tests must run locally and deterministically.
+
+### 16.3 Manual acceptance test
+
+A complete manual test should demonstrate:
+
+1. Start a new interview.
+2. Answer a question correctly.
+3. Answer a question with a missing concept.
+4. Receive a relevant follow-up.
+5. Trigger the hint flow.
+6. Complete the interview.
+7. View the final report.
+8. Repeat the flow with local evaluation and no AWS configuration.
+
+---
+
+## 17. Development and Execution
+
+### 17.1 Local setup
+
+Create and activate a virtual environment.
+
+**Windows PowerShell**
+
+```powershell
+py -3.12 -m venv .venv
+.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
+python -m pip install --upgrade pip
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+**Linux or macOS**
+
+```bash
+python3.12 -m venv .venv
+source .venv/bin/activate
+python -m pip install --upgrade pip
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+If the chosen Python version is not installed, install a supported version before creating the environment.
+
+### 17.2 Run tests
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest -q
+```
+
+### 17.3 Run the application
+
+```bash
+streamlit run app.py
+```
+
+### 17.4 Version control
+
+The `.gitignore` file must exclude at least:
+
+```gitignore
+.venv/
+__pycache__/
+.pytest_cache/
+.env
+*.pyc
+```
+
+Keep `.env.example` in the repository, but never commit `.env` or real AWS credentials.
+
+---
+
+## 18. Deployment and Demonstration
+
+### 18.1 Minimum deployment requirement
+
+The application must run locally with the documented setup commands. Public deployment is optional unless required by the final hackathon submission rules.
+
+### 18.2 Deployment constraints
+
+Before using a hosted environment:
+
+- Confirm the hosting platform supports the selected Python version.
+- Configure secrets through the platform's secure configuration mechanism.
+- Confirm AWS Region, IAM permissions, and model access.
+- Avoid assuming that local AWS credentials exist in the hosted environment.
+- Test local evaluation even when deployed.
+- Confirm whether the session-state behavior is suitable for the chosen hosting setup.
+
+### 18.3 Demo preparation
+
+The demo should use a known set of test questions and expected outcomes. Prepare both the Streamlit web application demonstration and the Alexa+ MCP Server tool interactions (using a local inspector or stdio client).
+
+Never fake a successful agent call or present mocked output as a live response.
+
+---
+
+## 19. Technical Decision Register
+
+| ID    | Decision                        | Rationale                                                                    | Revisit when                                                    |
+| ----- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| TD-01 | Python                          | Matches the developer's current learning path and supports rapid prototyping | Performance or platform constraints emerge                      |
+| TD-02 | Streamlit                       | Minimizes frontend implementation; provides rapid feedback                   | A separate frontend becomes necessary                           |
+| TD-03 | Modular monolith                | Easier to build, test, and debug than distributed services                   | The product grows substantially                                 |
+| TD-04 | JSON question bank              | Simple, reviewable, offline-friendly data source                             | Questions require persistent editing or concurrent management   |
+| TD-05 | Deterministic adaptive engine   | Predictable behavior, transparent explanations, and testability              | A measured improvement justifies a different approach           |
+| TD-06 | Local evaluator fallback        | Keeps the core experience available 100% offline without credentials         | Better offline semantic evaluation becomes necessary            |
+| TD-07 | Alexa+ MCP Server integration   | Realigns project directly with "Build, Ship, Shape" hackathon track          | Hackathon track or criteria change                              |
+| TD-08 | Streamlit session state         | Sufficient for a single-session prototype                                    | Persistent history or accounts become required                  |
+| TD-09 | No database in version 1        | Avoids setup and maintenance overhead                                        | Persistence becomes a product requirement                       |
+| TD-10 | MCP Standard Tools              | Exposes domain functions via open standard for Alexa+ agents                 | Alternative agent communication protocols emerge                |
+| TD-11 | Pytest for automated tests      | Simple, widely used Python test framework                                    | A broader testing architecture is needed                        |
+| TD-12 | Environment-based configuration | Keeps secrets and server port configs manageable                             | Deployment requires a managed secrets service                   |
+
+---
+
+## 20. Implementation Order
+
+Build in the following order. Do not start all modules at once.
+
+1. **Project setup:** Create the virtual environment, dependencies, repository, and file structure.
+2. **Question bank:** Write and validate 8–12 reviewed questions (`question_bank.json`).
+3. **Local evaluator:** Implement the 10-point rubric and validated evaluation result (`evaluator.py`).
+4. **Adaptive engine:** Implement deterministic follow-up selection and concept tracking (`adaptive_engine.py`).
+5. **Interview engine:** Connect questions, answers, evaluation, and progression (`interview_engine.py`).
+6. **Report generator:** Create comprehensive session report (`report_generator.py`).
+7. **Streamlit UI:** Build the start, interview, feedback, and report screens (`app.py`).
+8. **Alexa+ MCP Server:** Expose standardized MCP interview tools for Alexa+ agents (`mcp_server.py`).
+9. **Automated tests:** Verify complete test suite across all modules (`tests/`).
+10. **Documentation & QA:** Verify README, TRD, and factual friction log.
+
+The application should remain runnable at every major stage.
+
+---
+
+## 21. Definition of Technical Completion
+
+The technical implementation is ready for the final demo when:
+
+- [ ] The documented environment setup works cleanly.
+- [ ] The question bank loads and passes validation.
+- [ ] The complete interview flow works in local mode.
+- [ ] Evaluation results are validated before use.
+- [ ] Adaptive follow-ups match the defined rules.
+- [ ] The application prevents invalid question IDs and repeated-question loops.
+- [ ] The final report is generated correctly.
+- [ ] Automated tests pass across all components.
+- [ ] Alexa+ MCP Server exposes tested tools over stdio/SSE.
+- [ ] No real secrets are committed to the repository.
+- [ ] README instructions reproduce the local demo.
+- [ ] The friction log records actual observed problems rather than invented ones.
+- [ ] Any simulated functionality is clearly identified as simulated.
+
+---
+
+## 22. Open Decisions Before Final Submission
+
+These items should be verified rather than assumed:
+
+1. **Hackathon rules:** Confirm the current eligibility, deadline, and deliverables for the "Build, Ship, Shape" Alexa+ track.
+2. **Hosting:** Decide whether a public URL is required or a local demonstration with video is acceptable.
+3. **MCP Tool Integration:** Test tools against standard MCP inspector and document interaction traces.
+4. **Dependency versions:** Freeze the versions that have passed tests in the development environment.
+
+## Final technical recommendation
+
+Build a **single-process Python + Streamlit application with a JSON question bank, a deterministic adaptive engine, a validated local evaluator, and a self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Alexa+ Agent Skills**.
+
+This architecture gives you a working offline-capable core first, directly fulfills the "Build, Ship, Shape" Amazon Developer Hackathon primary track (Alexa+ MCP Agent Skills), and avoids adding infrastructure that does not directly improve the interview-coaching experience.

+## 1.1 Theme name: Focused Intelligence
+
+EduAgent Interview Coach uses a professional, light-first interface built around clarity, focused learning, and trustworthy feedback.

+The visual identity should communicate:

+- **Intelligence:** Structured information and clear hierarchy.
+- **Focus:** Minimal distractions while answering interview questions.
+- **Trust:** Transparent scores and understandable feedback.
+- **Progress:** Visible learning milestones without excessive gamification.
+- **Professionalism:** A polished environment suitable for students, mentors, and hackathon judges.

+2. One primary action should dominate each screen.
+3. Questions and answers must be easy to read.
+4. Feedback must distinguish strengths, gaps, and corrections.
+5. Scores must never rely on color alone.
+6. AI activity must be transparent and accurately labelled.
+7. Spacing, alignment, and typography must remain consistent.

+

+## 2.4 Color usage rules
+
+- Cobalt blue is the only primary action color.
+- Deep navy is the main brand and heading color.
+- Green indicates a positive state, not a high score by itself.
+- Amber indicates an incomplete or cautionary state, not a failure.
+- Red is reserved for errors and significant misconceptions.
+- Gray is used for neutral information.
+- Never color an entire page with a semantic status color.
+- Never communicate correctness through color alone; always include text or an icon.
+- Avoid gradients in the interface, including the main header and buttons.
+
+# 3. Typography System
+
+## 3.1 Locked fonts
+
+<box border radius="xl" padding={4} gap={3}>
+  <box gap={1}>
+    <text color="secondary" size="xs">PRIMARY UI FONT</text>
+    <title size="2xl">Inter</title>

+  </box>
+  <divider color="subtle" />

+    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Code snippets, operation names, complexity expressions, and technical examples.</text>
+  </box>
+</box>
+
+Font stacks:
+
+- Interface: `Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif`
+- Technical content: `JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, monospace`
+
+Use Inter as the default. Use the technical font sparingly, only when it improves readability.
+
+## 3.2 Type scale
+
+| Element | Size | Weight | Line height |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Main page title | 30 px | 700 | 38 px |
+| Section title | 24 px | 650 | 32 px |
+| Card title | 18 px | 600 | 26 px |
+| Question text | 22 px | 500–600 | 34 px |
+| Body text | 15 px | 400 | 24 px |
+| Button text | 14 px | 600 | 20 px |
+| Form label | 14 px | 600 | 20 px |
+| Supporting text | 13 px | 400 | 19 px |
+| Metadata | 12 px | 500 | 16 px |
+| Technical text | 13–14 px | 400–500 | 21 px |
+
+### Typography rules
+
+1. Do not use more than four text sizes in a single content section.
+2. Use sentence case, not all-uppercase headings.
+3. Use bold for emphasis, not entire paragraphs.
+4. Keep question text comfortably readable.
+5. Avoid light font weights for essential information.
+6. Do not use decorative or handwritten fonts.
+7. Avoid long lines of text; aim for approximately 60–80 characters per line in reading-heavy areas.
+
+# 4. Spacing and Layout System
+
+## 4.1 Base spacing scale
+
+Use an **8 px base rhythm** with 4 px for compact adjustments.
+
+| Token | Value | Intended use |
+|---|---:|---|
+| `space-1` | 4 px | Icon-to-label spacing, tiny adjustments |
+| `space-2` | 8 px | Compact internal gaps |
+| `space-3` | 12 px | Input label spacing and tight groups |
+| `space-4` | 16 px | Standard component gaps |
+| `space-5` | 20 px | Card content separation |
+| `space-6` | 24 px | Standard card padding |
+| `space-8` | 32 px | Section separation |
+| `space-10` | 40 px | Major content separation |
+| `space-12` | 48 px | Page section spacing |
+| `space-16` | 64 px | Large desktop-only separation |
+
+Use these values consistently. Avoid arbitrary spacing values unless required by a specific component.
+
+## 4.2 Page layout
+
+- Main page background: `#F6F7FB`.
+- Desktop content maximum width: `1200 px`.
+- Standard page horizontal padding: `32 px`.
+- Tablet horizontal padding: `24 px`.
+- Mobile horizontal padding: `16 px`.
+- Header height: `64 px`.
+- Standard card padding: `24 px`.
+- Compact card padding: `16 px`.
+- Major section gap: `32 px`.
+- Standard component gap: `16 px`.
+
+## 4.3 Grid and columns
+
+- Desktop: use a centered content container with a maximum width of 1200 px.
+- Tablet: reduce horizontal padding and keep content readable.
+- Mobile: use a single-column layout.
+- The main interview question should receive more space than secondary information.
+- Never force the answer editor into a narrow sidebar.
+- On small screens, stack the question, answer editor, feedback, and supporting panels vertically.
+
+# 5. Shape, Borders, and Shadows
+
+## 5.1 Border-radius scale
+
+| Component | Radius |
+|---|---:|
+| Small labels and chips | 6 px |
+| Input fields | 8 px |
+| Buttons | 8 px |
+| Standard cards | 12 px |
+| Main content panels | 16 px |
+| Dialogs and large overlays | 16 px |
+| Circular icons or avatars | 50% |
+
+**Locked rule:** Do not use pill-shaped buttons throughout the application. Use rounded rectangles to maintain a professional software-product appearance.
+
+## 5.2 Borders
+
+- Standard border: `1 px solid #E2E8F0`.
+- Emphasized border: `1 px solid #CBD5E1`.
+- Selected border: `1 px solid #315EFB`.
+- Avoid thick decorative borders.
+- Use borders to define structure, not to highlight every element.
+
+## 5.3 Shadows
+
+Use very subtle shadows only for floating elements, dropdowns, and dialogs.
+
+- Cards: no shadow by default.
+- Hovered interactive cards: a subtle shadow and/or border change.
+- Dialogs and dropdowns: soft shadow.
+- Do not use strong shadows around every card.
+- Do not use glassmorphism or glowing effects.
+
+# 6. Icon System
+
+## 6.1 Icon library
+
+Use **Lucide-style outline icons** consistently.
+
+All icons must follow the same visual style. Do not mix outline icons with colorful emoji, filled cartoon icons, and unrelated icon libraries.
+
+## 6.2 Icon sizes
+
+| Context | Size |
+|---|---:|
+| Inline status | 14–16 px |
+| Button icon | 16 px |
+| Navigation icon | 20 px |
+| Card illustration icon | 24 px |
+| Empty-state illustration | 32 px |
+
+Default stroke width: approximately 2 px.
+
+## 6.3 Approved icon mapping
+
+| Meaning | Icon |
+|---|---|
+| Application identity | `brain-circuit` |
+| Dashboard or home | `layout-dashboard` |
+| Interview | `messages-square` |
+| Question | `circle-help` |
+| Submit answer | `arrow-up` |
+| Hint | `lightbulb` |
+| Progress | `chart-no-axes-column-increasing` |
+| Correct answer | `check-circle-2` |
+| Missing concept | `alert-circle` |
+| Error | `x-circle` |
+| Information | `info` |
+| Time | `clock-3` |
+| Settings | `settings-2` |
+| Report | `file-text` |
+| Restart | `rotate-ccw` |
+| Next question | `arrow-right` |
+| AI evaluation | `sparkles` |
+| Local evaluation | `shield-check` |
+| External service | `cloud` |
+| Expand details | `chevron-down` |
+| Collapse details | `chevron-up` |
+
+Use the nearest available Lucide icon if a named icon is unavailable, but maintain the same outline style and meaning.
+
+## 6.4 Icon rules
+
+- Every icon-only button must have an accessible label.
+- Do not use an icon to replace an unclear text label.
+- Do not use emojis as application controls.
+- Use semantic status icons alongside text.
+- Do not decorate every heading with an icon.
+
+# 7. Buttons and Actions
+
+## 7.1 Primary button
+
+Used for the most important action on a screen.
+
+Examples: `Start interview`, `Submit answer`, `View report`.
+
+- Background: `#315EFB`
+- Text: `#FFFFFF`
+- Height: 44 px
+- Horizontal padding: 16 px
+- Radius: 8 px
+- Font: Inter, 14 px, weight 600
+
+Hover: `#254DE5`
+
+Pressed: `#1D43CB`
+
+Disabled: `#DCE3F5` background with `#64748B` text.
+
+## 7.2 Secondary button
+
+Used for helpful but non-primary actions.
+
+- Background: `#FFFFFF`
+- Text: `#172554`
+- Border: `1 px solid #CBD5E1`
+- Height: 44 px
+- Radius: 8 px
+
+Hover: `#F1F4F9`
+
+## 7.3 Tertiary button
+
+Used for low-emphasis actions such as `Cancel`, `Back`, or `Skip`.
+
+- Background: transparent.
+- Text: `#475569`.
+- No prominent border.
+- Height: 40–44 px.
+
+## 7.4 Destructive button
+
+Use only for actions that discard or clear meaningful information.
+
+- Background: `#B91C1C`.
+- Text: `#FFFFFF`.
+- Require confirmation when an action could discard an active session.
+
+## 7.5 Button behavior
+
+- Only one visually dominant primary action per screen.
+- Buttons must have clear hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and loading states.
+- Show a loading indicator when an operation is genuinely in progress.
+- Prevent duplicate submission while an answer is being evaluated.
+- Never display a successful state before the action has actually succeeded.
+
+# 8. Form and Answer Editor
+
+## 8.1 Text input styling
+
+- Background: `#FFFFFF`.
+- Border: `1 px solid #CBD5E1`.
+- Radius: 8 px.
+- Padding: 12 px.
+- Text size: 15 px.
+- Minimum height for single-line inputs: 44 px.
+
+Focus state:
+
+- Border: `#315EFB`.
+- Visible focus ring: `0 0 0 3px rgba(49, 94, 251, 0.16)`.
+
+Error state:
+
+- Border: `#B91C1C`.
+- Error text: `#991B1B`.
+- Include a short message explaining how to resolve the error.
+
+## 8.2 Interview answer editor
+
+The answer editor is one of the most important components in the product.
+
+- Full width of the primary question panel.
+- Minimum height: 180 px on desktop.
+- Minimum height: 160 px on mobile.
+- Text size: 15 px.
+- Line height: 24 px.
+- Padding: 16 px.
+- Background: `#FFFFFF`.
+- Border: `#CBD5E1`.
+- Radius: 12 px.
+
+Placeholder:
+
+> Explain your answer step by step. Include the key concepts and reasoning.
+
+The placeholder must disappear or become unobtrusive when the student begins typing.
+
+## 8.3 Input interaction rules
+
+- Preserve the answer during normal interface reruns.
+- Display a clear message for empty submissions.
+- Avoid unnecessary character restrictions.
+- Keep the submit action near the editor.
+- If evaluation fails, preserve the answer so the student does not need to retype it.
+- Do not clear the answer before a successful submission has been recorded.
+
+# 9. Card System
+
+## 9.1 Standard content card
+
+- Background: `#FFFFFF`.
+- Border: `1 px solid #E2E8F0`.
+- Radius: 12 px.
+- Padding: 24 px.
+- Gap between internal elements: 16 px.
+
+Use standard cards for questions, progress summaries, and reports.
+
+## 9.2 Question card
+
+- Background: `#FFFFFF`.
+- Border: `1 px solid #E2E8F0`.
+- Radius: 16 px.
+- Padding: 32 px on desktop and 20 px on mobile.
+- Question text: 22 px.
+- Metadata appears above the question, not mixed into its main text.
+- Avoid decorative illustrations inside the question area.
+
+## 9.3 Feedback card
+
+Use separate sections for:
+
+- What was correct.
+- What was missing.
+- What needs correction.
+- Recommended next step.
+
+Each section should have a short heading and concise content.
+
+Avoid placing all feedback into one large block of undifferentiated text.
+
+## 9.4 Card interaction
+
+Only cards that actually perform an action should look clickable.
+
+Clickable cards must have a hover state and keyboard focus state. Static information cards must not imitate buttons.
+
+# 10. Status Labels and Badges
+
+Use compact badges for question difficulty, evaluation mode, and progress state.
+
+| Badge | Appearance |
+|---|---|
+| Easy | Pale green background, dark green text |
+| Medium | Pale amber background, dark amber text |
+| Hard | Pale red background, dark red text |
+| Local evaluation | Neutral gray background, dark navy text |
+| AI evaluation | Pale blue background, dark blue text |
+| Completed | Pale green background, dark green text |
+| In progress | Pale blue background, dark blue text |
+
+Badge height: approximately 24 px.
+
+Horizontal padding: 8 px.
+
+Radius: 6 px.
+
+Text: 12 px, medium weight.
+
+Do not use badges for every piece of metadata. Use plain text when a badge does not improve understanding.
+
+# 11. Navigation and Header
+
+## 11.1 Header
+
+Height: 64 px.
+
+Background: `#FFFFFF`.
+
+Bottom border: `1 px solid #E2E8F0`.
+
+Contents:
+
+- Brand icon and product name on the left.
+- Current topic or session status where useful.
+- Evaluation mode indicator.
+- Settings or secondary actions only if implemented.
+
+Product name: **EduAgent Interview Coach**
+
+Do not add navigation items for features that do not exist.
+
+## 11.2 Brand treatment
+
+- Icon: `brain-circuit`, 24 px.
+- Icon background: `#E9EEFF`.
+- Icon foreground: `#315EFB`.
+- Wordmark: `#172554`, Inter, 16 px, weight 700.
+
+Do not create different logos or color variants for different screens.
+
+## 11.3 Navigation behavior
+
+For the first version, keep navigation minimal. The student should be able to start, continue, and finish an interview without navigating through a complex sidebar.
+
+If a sidebar is introduced later, use:
+
+- Width: 240 px on desktop.
+- Background: `#FFFFFF`.
+- Selected item: `#E9EEFF`.
+- Selected text and icon: `#315EFB`.
+- Unselected text: `#475569`.
+
+On mobile, replace the persistent sidebar with a compact navigation pattern only if the application actually needs additional destinations.
+
+# 12. Screen-by-Screen Theme
+
+## 12.1 Start screen
+
+**Purpose:** Explain the product and begin a session.
+
+Layout:
+- Centered content area, maximum width approximately 880 px.
+- Brand header at the top.
+- Clear page title.
+- Short supporting description.
+- One primary interview card.
+- A visible topic label: `DSA · Stacks & Queues`.
+- Role label: `Junior Software Developer`.
+- Evaluation mode indicator.
+- Primary button: `Start interview`.
+
+Use a white card against the `#F6F7FB` canvas.
+
+Do not use a large animated hero, a rotating carousel, or an oversized decorative AI illustration.
+
+## 12.2 Interview screen
+
+**Purpose:** Keep the student's attention on the current question.
+
+Desktop layout:
+- Main content width: approximately 760–840 px.
+- Progress and session metadata at the top.
+- Question card.
+- Answer editor directly below the question.
+- Hint and submit controls underneath the editor.
+
+Order:
+
+1. Progress indicator.
+2. Topic and difficulty.
+3. Question text.
+4. Answer editor.
+5. Hint action.
+6. Primary submit action.
+
+The submit button should be the most visually prominent control in the answer area.
+
+## 12.3 Feedback state
+
+**Purpose:** Make the evaluation understandable.
+
+Display:
+
+1. Score and short interpretation.
+2. Correct points.
+3. Missing concepts.
+4. Possible misconceptions, if present.
+5. Recommended next step.
+6. Reason for the selected follow-up.
+7. Continue action.
+
+Use semantic colors only on the relevant feedback sections. Keep the surrounding screen neutral.
+
+A score should be displayed as `7/10`, not as a large decorative circular gauge that consumes unnecessary space.
+
+## 12.4 Final report
+
+**Purpose:** Help the student understand performance and what to revise.
+
+Layout:
+- Page title: `Interview report`.
+- Overall score and attempts summary.
+- Demonstrated concepts.
+- Concepts to revisit.
+- Important misconceptions.
+- Recommended revision actions.
+- Evaluation mode disclosure.
+- Primary action: `Start new interview`.
+
+The report must reflect actual session data. Do not show empty charts or fabricated statistics simply to make the page look more advanced.
+
+## 12.5 Error and empty states
+
+Error states must be calm, specific, and actionable.
+
+Example:
+
+**Unable to evaluate this answer**
+
+The evaluation service did not return a valid result. Your answer is still available. You can retry or continue using local evaluation if it is available.
+
+Buttons:
+- `Retry evaluation`
+- `Use local evaluation` — only if the fallback is implemented.
+
+Do not display raw stack traces or technical credentials to the student.
+
+# 13. Progress Indicators and Scoring
+
+## 13.1 Progress bar
+
+- Track session progress only when a meaningful denominator is available.
+- Height: 6 px.
+- Track: `#E2E8F0`.
+- Fill: `#315EFB`.
+- Radius: 999 px.
+
+If the total number of questions is adaptive and unknown, show `Question 4` or `4 questions answered` rather than claiming that the session is 60% complete.
+
+## 13.2 Score presentation
+
+- Main score: 28–32 px, weight 700.
+- Maximum score: displayed beside the score.
+- Interpretation: short text beneath the score.
+- Correct, incomplete, and incorrect points must be explained in text.
+
+Do not classify students with stigmatizing labels such as “bad candidate” or “failure.”
+
+## 13.3 Mastery status
+
+Use these labels:
+
+- `Demonstrated`
+- `Needs practice`
+- `Not yet assessed`
+
+Do not mark a concept as mastered simply because it has been displayed or attempted.
+
+# 14. Motion and Interaction
+
+## 14.1 Motion policy
+
+The interface should feel responsive but not animated for decoration.
+
+- Button hover: 120–160 ms.
+- Card hover: 150 ms.
+- Small state transition: 150–200 ms.
+- Avoid large page transitions.
+- Avoid bouncing, pulsing, spinning decorative elements, and animated backgrounds.
+
+A spinner is permitted only while an actual operation is in progress.
+
+## 14.2 Loading states
+
+During evaluation:
+
+- Preserve the student's answer.
+- Disable duplicate submission.
+- Show a small spinner.
+- Use status text such as `Evaluating your answer…`.
+- Do not imply that an external AI call is occurring when local evaluation is running.
+
+## 14.3 Reduced motion
+
+If the user prefers reduced motion, avoid non-essential transitions and animations.
+
+# 15. Responsive Design Rules
+
+## 15.1 Breakpoints
+
+| Device class | Width |
+|---|---:|
+| Mobile | Up to 639 px |
+| Tablet | 640–1023 px |
+| Desktop | 1024 px and above |
+
+## 15.2 Mobile
+
+- One-column layout.
+- 16 px page padding.
+- 20 px question-card padding.
+- Full-width primary button where appropriate.
+- Answer editor at least 160 px high.
+- No horizontal scrolling.
+- Stack report cards vertically.
+- Keep all controls usable with touch.
+
+## 15.3 Tablet
+
+- 24 px page padding.
+- Main content width constrained for readability.
+- Two columns allowed only for compact summary sections.
+- Keep the interview question and editor in the primary column.
+
+## 15.4 Desktop
+
+- Maximum content width: 1200 px.
+- 32 px horizontal page padding.
+- Question and answer area centered.
+- Optional supporting panels may sit beside the main area, but must not compete with the question.
+
+# 16. Accessibility Requirements
+
+Target WCAG 2.2 AA principles where practical.
+
+- Maintain readable contrast for text and controls.
+- Provide visible keyboard focus.
+- Ensure buttons and fields have meaningful accessible names.
+- Do not communicate status through color alone.
+- Use labels for input fields rather than relying only on placeholders.
+- Ensure interactive targets are comfortably sized; aim for at least 44 × 44 px for primary touch controls.
+- Maintain logical heading order.
+- Avoid excessive motion.
+- Keep feedback readable at normal browser zoom.
+- Support keyboard navigation for the core interview flow.
+
+# 17. Empty States and Microcopy
+
+Use short, respectful, student-friendly language.
+
+| Situation | Recommended copy |
+|---|---|
+| No session yet | Ready to practice? Start your Stacks and Queues interview. |
+| Empty answer | Write an answer before submitting. |
+| Evaluation in progress | Evaluating your answer… |
+| Weak answer | Let's strengthen the fundamentals with a focused follow-up. |
+| Missing concept | Your answer is partly correct. Let's revisit one important concept. |
+| Strong answer | Good explanation. Let's move to the next concept. |
+| Session complete | Interview complete. Review your strengths and topics to revisit. |
+| Service unavailable | Evaluation is unavailable right now. Your answer has been preserved. |
+| Local mode active | Using local evaluation. Feedback may be less reliable for paraphrased answers. |
+| AI mode active | AI-assisted evaluation is enabled. Review feedback critically. |
+
+Do not promise that a student's next answer will be correct or that the application will guarantee interview success.
+
+# 18. Theme Consistency Rules
+
+These rules are mandatory for every screen.
+
+1. Use the locked color tokens only.
+2. Use Inter for interface text and JetBrains Mono for technical snippets.
+3. Use the defined spacing scale.
+4. Use the approved outline icon style.
+5. Keep cards white with subtle borders.
+6. Keep the main background light and neutral.
+7. Use cobalt blue for primary actions.
+8. Use semantic colors only for meaningful states.
+9. Keep the question and answer editor as the primary visual focus.
+10. Use consistent component sizes across all screens.
+11. Do not introduce dark mode in version 1.
+12. Do not add glassmorphism, neon effects, excessive gradients, or decorative charts.
+13. Do not introduce a new font, icon pack, or unrelated accent color without formally revising this document.
+14. Any design revision must update this file before the revised style is implemented across the product.
+
+# 19. Final Design Lock
+
+The following decisions are frozen for version 1:
+

+
+## Final instruction
+
+Treat this document as the single source of truth for the application's visual design. Implement the design consistently rather than redesigning individual screens independently.
+

+# EduAgent Interview Coach
+
+**EduAgent Interview Coach** is an adaptive, text-based technical interview practice web application designed for students and junior software developers preparing for Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) interviews and viva examinations.
+
+The initial version focuses on **Stacks and Queues**, using a closed-loop learning process: **assess, identify a gap, practice the gap, and reassess**.
+
+---
+
+## Features
+
+- **Reviewed Question Bank:** 8–12 reviewed DSA interview questions for Stacks and Queues with explicit concept tags, hints, and follow-up relationships.
+- **Consistent 10-Point Scoring Rubric:**
+  - Technical Correctness: 0–4
+  - Key Concepts: 0–3
+  - Reasoning: 0–2
+  - Clarity: 0–1
+- **Deterministic Adaptive Engine:** Selects targeted follow-ups based on identified gaps (strong responses progress, incomplete answers receive targeted follow-ups, and weak answers receive scaffolded assistance).
+- **Session Progress & Mastery Tracking:** Tracks demonstrated concepts, missing concepts, and attempted questions without infinite loops.
+- **Actionable Final Report:** Summarizes performance, demonstrated concepts, topics to revisit, and concrete revision recommendations.
+- **Reliable Local Offline Evaluation:** Fully functional without cloud credentials or internet access.
+- **Alexa+ MCP Agent Skill:** Exposes a self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server allowing Alexa+ agents to conduct interactive interview prep, query candidate weak spots, and generate revision reports.
+
+---
+

+

+"""
+EduAgent Interview Coach — Adaptive Question Selection & Mastery Engine
+========================================================================
+
+Implements deterministic, rule-based adaptive follow-up selection and
+session concept mastery tracking matching PRD Section 10.2 and TRD Section 9.
+
+Key design guarantees:
+1. Deterministic: Given the same session state and evaluation, the same next
+   question and explanation are always selected.
+2. Loop-free: Questions already asked in the active session are strictly excluded.
+3. Fallback-safe: If preferred follow-ups are exhausted, it gracefully falls back
+   to alternative bank questions or signals interview completion.
+4. Explainable: Returns user-friendly rationale explaining why each question was selected.
+"""
+
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple, Union
+
+
+class AdaptiveDecision:
+    """
+    Represents the output of the adaptive selection engine.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        next_question: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
+        internal_reason: str,
+        student_explanation: str,
+    ):
+        self.next_question = next_question
+        self.internal_reason = internal_reason
+        self.student_explanation = student_explanation
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "next_question_id": self.next_question["id"] if self.next_question else None,
+            "internal_reason": self.internal_reason,
+            "student_explanation": self.student_explanation,
+        }
+
+
+class AdaptiveEngine:
+    """
+    Coordinates question progression and concept mastery tracking.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, question_bank: Optional[Union[List[Dict[str, Any]], Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]]] = None):
+        """
+        Initialize the adaptive engine with an optional question bank.
+        Accepts either a list of question dicts or a mapping of id -> question dict.
+        """
+        self._bank_map: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
+        if question_bank is not None:
+            self.set_question_bank(question_bank)
+
+    def set_question_bank(self, question_bank: Union[List[Dict[str, Any]], Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]]) -> None:
+        """Loads or updates the active question bank."""
+        if isinstance(question_bank, dict):
+            self._bank_map = dict(question_bank)
+        elif isinstance(question_bank, list):
+            self._bank_map = {q["id"]: q for q in question_bank if isinstance(q, dict) and "id" in q}
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid question_bank type: {type(question_bank).__name__}")
+
+    def get_question_by_id(self, question_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Retrieve question dict by ID."""
+        return self._bank_map.get(question_id)
+
+    def update_concept_tracking(
+        self,
+        current_question: Dict[str, Any],
+        evaluation: Dict[str, Any],
+        demonstrated_concepts: Set[str],
+        unresolved_concepts: Set[str],
+    ) -> Tuple[Set[str], Set[str]]:
+        """
+        Updates session-level concept mastery based on evaluation outcome.
+        
+        Rules:
+        - Score >= 8 and no critical misconceptions:
+            Concepts of current question are marked demonstrated and removed from unresolved.
+        - Score < 8, or missing concepts, or misconceptions present:
+            Missing concepts and misconceptions are added to unresolved concepts.
+        """
+        score = evaluation.get("score", 0)
+        misconceptions = evaluation.get("misconceptions", [])
+        missing = evaluation.get("missing_concepts", [])
+        question_concepts = set(current_question.get("concepts", []))
+
+        # Check for strong mastery
+        if score >= 8 and len(misconceptions) == 0:
+            demonstrated_concepts.update(question_concepts)
+            # Remove any concepts now demonstrated
+            unresolved_concepts.difference_update(question_concepts)
+        else:
+            # Add identified gaps to unresolved
+            for item in missing:
+                unresolved_concepts.add(item)
+            for item in misconceptions:
+                unresolved_concepts.add(f"Misconception: {item}")
+            # If weak answer (score <= 4), track current question concepts as needing work
+            if score <= 4:
+                for c in question_concepts:
+                    if c not in demonstrated_concepts:
+                        unresolved_concepts.add(c)
+
+        return demonstrated_concepts, unresolved_concepts
+
+    def select_next_question(
+        self,
+        current_question: Dict[str, Any],
+        evaluation: Dict[str, Any],
+        asked_question_ids: Union[Set[str], List[str]],
+        question_bank: Optional[Union[List[Dict[str, Any]], Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]]] = None,
+    ) -> AdaptiveDecision:
+        """
+        Selects the next interview question deterministically based on student performance.
+
+        Parameters:
+            current_question: The question just completed.
+            evaluation: The validated evaluation result from evaluator.py.
+            asked_question_ids: IDs already presented in the current session (to prevent repetition).
+            question_bank: Optional override for the question bank.
+
+        Returns:
+            AdaptiveDecision with next_question, internal_reason, and student_explanation.
+        """
+        if question_bank is not None:
+            self.set_question_bank(question_bank)
+
+        if not self._bank_map:
+            return AdaptiveDecision(
+                next_question=None,
+                internal_reason="bank_empty",
+                student_explanation="Question bank is empty.",
+            )
+
+        asked_set = set(asked_question_ids)
+        score = evaluation.get("score", 0)
+        action = evaluation.get("recommended_action", "targeted_follow_up")
+        misconceptions = evaluation.get("misconceptions", [])
+        missing_concepts = evaluation.get("missing_concepts", [])
+
+        # Priority candidates from current question metadata
+        direct_follow_ups = [
+            qid for qid in current_question.get("follow_up_ids", [])
+            if qid in self._bank_map and qid not in asked_set
+        ]
+        fallback_id = current_question.get("fallback_follow_up_id")
+        fallback_candidate = (
+            self._bank_map[fallback_id]
+            if fallback_id and fallback_id in self._bank_map and fallback_id not in asked_set
+            else None
+        )
+
+        current_difficulty = current_question.get("difficulty", "medium")
+        current_topic = current_question.get("topic", "Stacks")
+
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        # Path A: Strong response (Score >= 8, action == "progress")
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        if action == "progress" or (score >= 8 and not misconceptions):
+            # Prefer higher difficulty or equal difficulty among direct follow-ups
+            candidate = self._pick_progressive_candidate(direct_follow_ups, current_difficulty)
+
+            if candidate:
+                diff_label = candidate.get("difficulty", "next")
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=candidate,
+                    internal_reason="mastery_demonstrated",
+                    student_explanation=f"Great explanation! Advancing to a {diff_label}-level question on {candidate.get('topic', current_topic)}.",
+                )
+
+            # If direct follow-ups exhausted, pick unasked question of higher difficulty or other topic
+            candidate = self._find_unasked_progressive_in_bank(asked_set, current_topic)
+            if candidate:
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=candidate,
+                    internal_reason="mastery_demonstrated_alternative",
+                    student_explanation="Solid grasp of this concept. Moving to explore the next topic area.",
+                )
+
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        # Path B: Critical misconception / Foundational gap (Score <= 4, action == "scaffold_hint")
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        elif action == "scaffold_hint" or score <= 4 or len(misconceptions) > 0:
+            # 1. Prefer fallback question if it exists and hasn't been asked
+            if fallback_candidate:
+                misconception_note = misconceptions[0] if misconceptions else "this foundational concept"
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=fallback_candidate,
+                    internal_reason="critical_misconception" if misconceptions else "foundational_gap",
+                    student_explanation=f"Selected a foundational question to help clarify: {misconception_note}.",
+                )
+
+            # 2. Prefer an easy question on the same topic
+            easy_candidate = self._find_unasked_by_criteria(asked_set, topic=current_topic, difficulty="easy")
+            if easy_candidate:
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=easy_candidate,
+                    internal_reason="foundational_scaffold",
+                    student_explanation=f"Let's step back and reinforce the fundamentals of {current_topic}.",
+                )
+
+            # 3. Any direct follow-up
+            if direct_follow_ups:
+                candidate = self._bank_map[direct_follow_ups[0]]
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=candidate,
+                    internal_reason="scaffold_fallback",
+                    student_explanation="Let's practice a related aspect of this data structure.",
+                )
+
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        # Path C: Partial understanding (Score 5-7, action == "targeted_follow_up")
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        else:
+            gap_summary = missing_concepts[0] if missing_concepts else "key operation mechanics"
+
+            # 1. Look for direct follow-up that addresses the missing concept
+            matching_direct = self._find_follow_up_matching_concepts(direct_follow_ups, missing_concepts)
+            if matching_direct:
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=matching_direct,
+                    internal_reason="targeted_follow_up",
+                    student_explanation=f"Follow-up selected to practice: {gap_summary}.",
+                )
+
+            # 2. Any direct follow-up
+            if direct_follow_ups:
+                candidate = self._bank_map[direct_follow_ups[0]]
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=candidate,
+                    internal_reason="targeted_follow_up",
+                    student_explanation=f"Follow-up selected to reinforce: {gap_summary}.",
+                )
+
+            # 3. Fallback candidate
+            if fallback_candidate:
+                return AdaptiveDecision(
+                    next_question=fallback_candidate,
+                    internal_reason="targeted_fallback",
+                    student_explanation=f"Practicing related principles for {current_topic}.",
+                )
+
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        # Exhaustion & General Bank Fallback (Loop Prevention)
+        # -------------------------------------------------------------
+        # If no specific follow-up matched, pick any unasked question in the bank
+        general_candidate = self._find_any_unasked(asked_set, preferred_topic=current_topic)
+        if general_candidate:
+            return AdaptiveDecision(
+                next_question=general_candidate,
+                internal_reason="bank_coverage",
+                student_explanation=f"Next question selected to broaden coverage of {general_candidate.get('topic', 'DSA')}.",
+            )
+
+        # All questions in bank have been asked
+        return AdaptiveDecision(
+            next_question=None,
+            internal_reason="interview_complete",
+            student_explanation="All interview questions have been completed! Generating your final report.",
+        )
+
+    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Internal Helpers
+    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def _pick_progressive_candidate(
+        self, candidate_ids: List[str], current_difficulty: str
+    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Picks a follow-up prioritizing harder or equal difficulty."""
+        diff_rank = {"easy": 1, "medium": 2, "hard": 3}
+        current_rank = diff_rank.get(current_difficulty, 2)
+
+        higher = []
+        equal = []
+        lower = []
+
+        for qid in candidate_ids:
+            q = self._bank_map[qid]
+            rank = diff_rank.get(q.get("difficulty", "medium"), 2)
+            if rank > current_rank:
+                higher.append(q)
+            elif rank == current_rank:
+                equal.append(q)
+            else:
+                lower.append(q)
+
+        if higher:
+            return higher[0]
+        if equal:
+            return equal[0]
+        if lower:
+            return lower[0]
+        return None
+
+    def _find_follow_up_matching_concepts(
+        self, candidate_ids: List[str], missing_concepts: List[str]
+    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Finds candidate whose concept tags overlap with missing concepts."""
+        missing_lower = {m.lower() for m in missing_concepts}
+        for qid in candidate_ids:
+            q = self._bank_map[qid]
+            for concept in q.get("concepts", []):
+                if any(m in concept.lower() or concept.lower() in m for m in missing_lower):
+                    return q
+        return None
+
+    def _find_unasked_by_criteria(
+        self, asked_set: Set[str], topic: Optional[str] = None, difficulty: Optional[str] = None
+    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Finds any unasked question matching topic and/or difficulty."""
+        for q in self._bank_map.values():
+            if q["id"] in asked_set:
+                continue
+            if topic and q.get("topic") != topic:
+                continue
+            if difficulty and q.get("difficulty") != difficulty:
+                continue
+            return q
+        return None
+
+    def _find_unasked_progressive_in_bank(
+        self, asked_set: Set[str], current_topic: str
+    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Finds unasked question in bank, switching topic or increasing difficulty."""
+        other_topic = "Queues" if current_topic == "Stacks" else "Stacks"
+        # Try other topic first for balanced interview
+        candidate = self._find_unasked_by_criteria(asked_set, topic=other_topic)
+        if candidate:
+            return candidate
+        # Try harder on current topic
+        candidate = self._find_unasked_by_criteria(asked_set, topic=current_topic, difficulty="hard")
+        if candidate:
+            return candidate
+        # Any remaining on current topic
+        return self._find_unasked_by_criteria(asked_set, topic=current_topic)
+
+    def _find_any_unasked(
+        self, asked_set: Set[str], preferred_topic: Optional[str] = None
+    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        """Finds any unasked question, preferring preferred_topic if available."""
+        if preferred_topic:
+            for q in self._bank_map.values():
+                if q["id"] not in asked_set and q.get("topic") == preferred_topic:
+                    return q
+        for q in self._bank_map.values():
+            if q["id"] not in asked_set:
+                return q
+        return None
